4: **Who builds it:** this project, in this workspace. No Gemini, Mistral, ChatGPT, Figma, Suno, or other AI product is part of the build.

Covers product, market, competitors, marketing, operations, and information systems. |
16: | Jingle | `audio/stamp-jingle.mp3` | Plays, 15–60 seconds, names Stamp and the toast-sticker idea. |
17: | Website | Vercel production URL | Loads with no login. Landing page for Stamp. |
18: | Chatbot | `{site}/chat` | Same deployment. Answers product questions from the locked spec. No login. |
19: | Video | `.mp4` you record from the slide deck we build | Talking-head, 2–3 minutes, hard stop 3:29. Pitch finishes by 1:00. |
20: | Chat-session form | Learn form | Still a graded item. We submit the link to this project’s sessions. It is not a separate production stage. |
21: 
22: Missing the video scores 0/25. Missing the chat-session form scores an E. The PDF, jingle, site, and chatbot are the other four core items.

27:

29: 
30: | Item | Decision |
31: | --- | --- |
32: | Brand and product name | **Stamp** |
33: | Format | A thin, single-serve disc of spread on a food-safe release film, nested in a printed card sheet. Peel, press onto hot toast, done. |
34: | Category in the dataset | Spreads |
35: | Launch line | Four flavours, locked with you: Salted Butter, Raspberry, Yeast extract, Peanut. |
36: | Packs | An 8-stamp sheet of one flavour (10 g each, 80 g), and a mixed sheet with two of each. $5.00 a sheet. |
37: | Buyer | Someone who eats toast away from a full kitchen: a flat, an office, a hall, a school bag. They want flavour without a knife or a jar. |
38: | Position | Pantry-stable for 12 months. $5.00 a sheet is $6.25 per 100 g, above about 90% of branded spread SKUs. |
39: | Allergen we will state | Peanut contains peanuts. Salted Butter is dairy. Yeast extract contains gluten from barley. Full list is in `brand/product-spec.md`. |
40: | Claims we will make | Peel-and-press, one portion, even cover, four flavours, no knife. |
41: | Claims we will not make | Health treatment, organic, gluten-free, low-sugar, or “better for you,” unless a finished recipe actually supports that sentence. No fake certification marks on the pack. |

Industrial constraints: target cost per stamp, ambient or chilled shelf life, and the claim ban from the table above.

83:    - A row is name + brand + weight + quarter. Same name with two weights is two SKUs.
84:    - Replace unit prices above $40 when units and revenue imply a normal shelf price (`revenue ÷ units`). Log each replacement.
85:    - Impute a missing revenue or units only when the surviving price makes the identity `price × units ≈ revenue` hold.
86:    - Parse weight into grams and pack count.
87: 3. Recompute spreads revenue and units by year, by price tier, and by brand. Build three PNG figures in `data/figures/`:
88:    - Quarterly spreads revenue, 2022-Q1 through 2025-Q4, with the other three categories as context.
89:    - 2022 vs 2025 spreads revenue by price tier.
90:    - Price per 100 g for branded spreads, with the Stamp sheet price marked once it is chosen.
91: 4. Set the sheet price and the mixed-sheet price from that per-100 g band. Record both in the product spec.

93: **Done when:** the spec has recipes, prices, and claims; the three PNGs exist; every number on them matches the cleaned CSV.

95: ## Stage 2 — Logo, pack, and social ad
96: 
97: **Produces:** the three images the PDF and the site share.
98: 
99: Visual system, fixed before generation:
100: 
101: - Wordmark: STAMP, all capitals. A custom drawing in the Toundra construction (heavy stems, round feet, semicircular arches). No symbol.
102: - One colour pair on every flavour: light purple `#E24BFF` and dark purple `#3B0764`. Dark on light, the same relationship as Toundra's forest green on lime. Flavour is type, not a second colour.
103: - Manrope is the text face only. It is not the wordmark.
104: - Pack: flat front. Forest field, purple STAMP, flavour name, and the line “Peel. Press. Toast.”
105: - Ad: 4:5, purple field, STAMP, and the same line.
106: 
107: Generation order: logo first, then pack and ad using the logo as the reference image so the mark matches. Save the final files as `brand/logo.png`, `brand/pack.png`, and `brand/ad.png`. Keep the earlier frames in `brand/explorations/` so the finals are the ones the other stages use.
108: 
109: **Done when:** the three finals show the same name, the same four flavours, and no certification badges we do not hold.
110: 
111: ## Stage 3 — Jingle
112: 
113: **Produces:** `audio/stamp-jingle.mp3`.
114: 
115: Built locally. No music-generation service.
116: 
117: 1. Write a 20–40 second lyric in `audio/lyrics.txt`. The hook says “Stamp” and the action peel / press / toast. One flavour can be named. Tone matches the pack: short, bright, not a wellness ad.
118: 2. Render a melody and a simple drum bed in Python (numpy) and mix a vocal with a local speech engine (`espeak-ng` or `festival`). Export with ffmpeg.
119: 3. Measure the file with `ffprobe`. Trim or rewrite until the duration is inside 15–60 seconds and the product name is intelligible.
120: 
121: **Done when:** the mp3 plays on its own, the duration check passes, and the lyric file matches the recording.
122: 
123: ## Stage 4 — Process diagram and ERD
124: 
125: **Produces:** the two figures the PDF still needs, plus the facts printed next to them.
126: 
127: 1. Pick one real New Zealand company that can deposit or portion-pack a spread. Record the trading name, the page the contact details came from, the location, and why the process fits a film-and-sheet format. Save this in `diagrams/manufacturer.md`.
128: 2. Critical process: **sheet making and release** — order in, batch deposit onto film, cut, nest, check, pack, dispatch. That is the process whose failure means a customer gets no breakfast. Draw it as a Mermaid flowchart with one failure path (failed weight check or film that will not release). Export `diagrams/process.png`. Write two bottlenecks and the operational response under the figure notes.
129: 3. Business-level entities: Product (flavour), Sheet (the sellable pack), Customer, Order, Order line, Batch, Manufacturer, Campaign. Five KPIs, each with a formula and the entity it comes from:
130:    - repeat purchase rate
131:    - stamps per order
132:    - on-time dispatch rate
133:    - batch rejection rate
134:    - gross margin per sheet after manufacturer cost
135: 4. Mermaid `erDiagram` to `diagrams/erd.png`. Short note on two questions this model can answer (which flavour is reordered, which batch failed release) and one it cannot (a medical effect).
136: 
137: **Done when:** both PNGs render cleanly, the manufacturer contact is copied from a page we opened, and the KPI list matches the ERD entities.
138: 
139: ## Stage 5 — Business plan PDF
140: 
141: **Produces:** `business-plan/Stamp-business-plan.pdf`.
142: 
143: A Python build script (`business-plan/build_pdf.py`, reportlab) lays the document out. Copy lives in `business-plan/copy.md` so the word count is checkable before export. Images are placed by the script from the paths above, not pasted by hand into a chat export.
144: 
145: | Section | Words | Content |
146: | --- | --- | --- |
147: | Cover | — | STAMP wordmark, logo, your name, date |
148: | Executive summary | 180–220 | Format, buyer, the spreads growth result, the jar-vs-stamp difference |
149: | Product | 300–400 | Four flavours, both recipes in brief, pack, price, how to use |
150: | Market | 300–400 | Cleaned figures and what they justify. Units labelled as NZD, not “thousands” left ambiguous. |
151: | Competitors | 250–350 | Three jar competitors with a sourced price, pack size, and the format difference |
152: | Customer and brand | 150–200 | Buyer, logo, pack shot, the line of ad copy |
153: | Marketing | 250–350 | Channel (Instagram and short video), the ad, where the jingle runs, two or three real NZ podcasts whose pages we opened |
154: | Operations | 200–280 | Manufacturer, the sheet-making process, the diagram, two bottlenecks |
155: | Information | 200–280 | Five KPIs, the ERD, two decisions the data supports |
156: | First 90 days | 80–120 | Assumptions labelled as assumptions |
157: 
158: Word count is the prose only. The script fails the build if the count falls outside 1,500–2,500. After export, render the PDF pages to images and read them: spelling of STAMP, figure legibility, no empty boxes, captions that state a conclusion.
159: 
160: **Done when:** the PDF builds in one command, the word-count check passes, and all six image types are visible in the rendered pages.
161: 
162: ## Stage 6 — Website (SvelteKit)
163: 
164: **Produces:** a SvelteKit app in `website/` that we can deploy.
165: 
166: | Choice | Spec |
167: | --- | --- |
168: | Framework | SvelteKit, TypeScript |
169: | Adapter | `@sveltejs/adapter-vercel` |
170: | Styling | Project CSS. Palette and type from Stage 2. No component library. |
171: | Rendering | Marketing routes prerendered. |
172: | Assets | Logo, pack, and ad copied into `website/static/` from `brand/`. |
173: | Copy | Pulled from `brand/product-spec.md`. The site does not add claims the spec forbids. |
174: 
175: Routes:
176: 
177: | Path | Page |
178: | --- | --- |
179: | `/` | Landing. What a Stamp is, the peel-press-toast sequence, the four flavours, the sheet price, one market sentence, the pack image. |
180: | `/flavours` | One block per flavour: name, taste, allergen, which sheet it is on. |
181: | `/chat` | Built in Stage 7. Linked in the header from the start so the nav does not change after deploy. |
182: 
183: No cart and no payment. The call to action is the product explanation and the support chat. A fake checkout is out of scope.
184: 
185: **Done when:** `npm run build` succeeds, `/` and `/flavours` show the real pack and the locked prices, and a logged-out browser can read both.
186: 
187: ## Stage 7 — Support chatbot
188: 
189: **Produces:** `/chat` on the same app. The public chatbot URL is the site URL plus `/chat`.
190: 
191: The bot is ours. It does not call another model at runtime.
192: 
193: - Knowledge is a typed module, `website/src/lib/knowledge.ts`, authored from the product spec: what a Stamp is, how to apply it, the four flavours, allergens, prices, pack contents, where it will be sold (direct, at launch), and a crushed-sheet complaint reply.
194: - Matching is intentional and small: normalise the question, score it against those topics, return the authored answer. A question that does not match gets a short reply listing what the bot can answer.
195: - Hard refusals, also authored: medical advice, and any “is it organic / gluten-free / low-sugar?” question, which is answered with the claim ban.
196: - The page looks like a support chat: a transcript, a text field, Stamp’s voice in short sentences.
197: 
198: Test list, saved as a run we can repeat:
199: 
200: 1. What is a Stamp?
201: 2. How do I use it?
202: 3. What flavours are there?
203: 4. Does the Peanut stamp contain nuts?
204: 5. Is it gluten-free?
205: 6. How much is a sheet?
206: 7. Where can I buy it?
207: 8. My sheet arrived crushed.
208: 9. Will this help my stomach?
209: 10. How does it compare with a jar of peanut butter?
210: 
211: **Done when:** those ten questions return the spec’s answers, questions 5 and 9 stay inside the claim ban, and the page is reachable at `/chat`.
212: 
213: ## Stage 8 — Deploy on Vercel
214: 
215: **Produces:** a production URL with no login.
216: 
217: 1. Vercel project, root directory `website`, framework SvelteKit, adapter already set.
218: 2. Production deploy from this project.
219: 3. Open the production origin and `/chat` in a private window. Confirm images load, prices match the PDF, and one chat question is answered.
220: 4. Write both URLs into `business-plan/urls.txt` and into the executive summary if the PDF is rebuilt after deploy. Rebuild the PDF if the summary names the URL.
221: 
222: **Done when:** the private-window check passes on the production host, not on `localhost`.
223: 
224: You will need to be logged in to Vercel for the deploy. The app itself does not ask a visitor to log in.
225: 
226: ## Stage 9 — Video package
227: 
228: **Produces:** a slide deck you record. The recording has to be you.
229: 
230: We build `presentation/Stamp-pitch.pptx` and `presentation/timing.md`.
231: 
232: | Time | Slides | Content we prepare |
233: | --- | --- | --- |
234: | 0:00–0:10 | Title | Stamp, your name. Does not count toward the two pitch slides. |
235: | 0:10–0:30 | Pitch 1 | The sticker format and the four flavours. |
236: | 0:30–1:00 | Pitch 2 | The spreads growth number from Stage 1, and the difference versus a jar. |
237: | 1:00–2:50 | 2–4 reflection slides | Slide shells and the two questions only. |
238: 
239: Pitch speaker notes are written to those times. You record with PowerPoint’s Record Slide Show, or any webcam-plus-slides recording, and export `.mp4`. Target length 2:30–2:50. Stop before 3:29.
240: 
241: The reflection answers stay in your voice: a specific moment from this build, and one critique of using AI to create the business. We leave those slides unwritten so the reflection you submit is yours.
242: 
243: **Done when:** the deck exists, the pitch notes fit in 60 seconds when read aloud, and you have an `.mp4` under 3:29 with your face and the slides in frame.
244: 
245: ## Stage 10 — Submission pack
246: 
247: On the morning of 16 October:
248: 
249: - Upload the PDF, the mp3, and the mp4 as files.
250: - Submit the Vercel URL and the `/chat` URL on the Learn form.
251: - Submit this project’s session link on the chat-session form.
252: - Open the production site once more in a private window before you send it.
253: 
254: ---
255: 
256: ## Stage order
257: 
258: ```text
259: 1 Product spec + cleaned data + market figures
260:         │
261:         ├── 2 Logo, pack, ad
262:         ├── 3 Jingle
263:         └── 4 Manufacturer, process PNG, ERD PNG
264:                  │
265:                  ▼
266:             5 Business plan PDF
267:                  │
268:                  ▼
269:             6 SvelteKit site ── 7 /chat bot ── 8 Vercel
270:                                                    │
271:                                                    ▼
272:                                             9 Slides and your recording
273:                                                    │
274:                                                    ▼
275:                                             10 Submit
276: ```
277: 
278: Stages 2, 3, and 4 can run as soon as Stage 1 has locked the name, the flavours, and the claims. The PDF waits until their files exist. The site waits until the logo and pack exist. The bot waits until the spec’s prices and allergens are final. Deploy is the last software step. The video is last because the pitch numbers have to match the PDF.
279: 
280: ## What you do, and what this build does
281: 
282: | You | This build |
283: | --- | --- |
284: | Vercel login when we deploy | The SvelteKit app, the bot, the deploy setup |
285: | Record and export the talking-head video | The deck, the pitch notes, the timing |
286: | Speak the reflection in your own words | The reflection slide shells and the two questions |
287: | Click submit on Learn | The PDF, mp3, site, and chat URL |

6: 
7: The buyer eats toast away from a full kitchen: a flat, an office, a hall, or a bag. They want a decided portion, not a jar to carry or a knife to wash.

9: Cleaned New Zealand sales put spreads at about $275 million NZD in 2022 and about $341 million NZD in 2025, about 24% growth. Premium grew faster than value, from about $88 million NZD to about $113 million, against value at about $36 million to about $39 million.

The sheet prints the flavour name and then the word spread, because butter on its own is a dairy-identity standard in Australia and New Zealand. The sold disc is cultured butterfat and salt, 2 g of salt to 78 g of fat, with no added oil. It contains milk. The home batch is that salt ratio beaten into softened butter, chilled, and eaten within 7 days.
18: 
19: Raspberry is raspberries, caster sugar, and lemon juice cooked down. The home batch reduces 120 g of fruit, 30 g of sugar, and 5 g of lemon juice to 80 g. The sold disc is that paste at 10 g. The label says 150 g of raspberries per 100 g because of the reduction.
20: 
21: Yeast extract is our paste. It is not Marmite and it is not Vegemite, and those names are not on the pack. The home batch is yeast extract, tomato paste, black treacle, and salt. The sold formula is yeast extract 80%, barley malt extract 15.5%, salt 2.5%, and vegetable concentrate 2%. It contains gluten from barley.
22: 
23: Peanut contains peanuts. The home paste is roasted peanuts and salt, ground and portioned before the oil separates. The sold disc is roasted peanuts 96%, vegetable fat 2.3% so the oil does not separate over 12 months, and salt 1.7%.
24: 
25: Every sheet, including Raspberry, is made in a facility that handles milk and peanuts. The mixed sheet contains milk, gluten, and peanuts. Nutrition figures on the backs are calculated from these proportions and from published composition tables. They are not a laboratory assay, and this plan does not present them as tested. No certification mark is used.
26: 
27: Making is the same shape for each flavour. Deposit 10 g, give or take 0.5 g, onto release film, cut the disc, nest eight in the card, and flow-wrap. A failed weight check, or a film that will not release, is a rejected stamp, not a sheet that ships. To use one, keep the sheet in a pantry, peel a stamp, press it onto hot toast, and wait a few seconds.
28: 
29: ## Market
30: 
31: These figures come from the cleaned sales file, not the raw spreadsheet totals. Money is in million NZD. The source column was stored in thousands of NZD and has been scaled so the unit is written out.
32: 
33: Spreads revenue was about $275 million NZD in 2022, about $305 million in 2023, about $319 million in 2024, and about $341 million in 2025. From 2022 to 2025 that is about 24% growth. The 2024 total sits a little above the raw column because blank revenue cells in that year were filled.
34: 
35: Value spreads moved from about $36 million NZD to about $39 million. Premium moved from about $88 million to about $113 million. Standard, still the largest tier, moved from about $151 million to about $189 million. Premium's rate of growth was faster than value's. Standard added the most dollars. A sheet priced like a value jar would be aimed at the slow part of the category. Stamp is priced above ordinary jars, toward a tier that grew, and away from where most of the money still sits.
36: 
37: :::figure
38: src: data/figures/02-spreads-revenue-by-tier-2022-vs-2025.png
39: caption: Premium revenue rose faster than value revenue, and standard remained the largest tier.
40: :::
41: 
42: On price per 100 g, 168 branded SKUs give a 10th percentile of $1.46 NZD, a median of $2.15, a 75th percentile of $2.77, and a 90th percentile of $5.19. The far tail is manuka honey, not peanut butter or jam. Fix & Fogg's SKU medians in the cleaned file sit around $2.65 per 100 g. The Stamp sheet is $6.25 per 100 g, above that 90th percentile. The price is the portion film and the card. It is not a claim that the paste is a luxury version of the median jar.
43: 
44: :::figure
45: src: data/figures/03-branded-spreads-price-per-100g.png
46: caption: At $6.25 NZD per 100 g, the Stamp sheet sits to the right of almost every branded spread in this chart.
47: :::
48: 
49: The file holds 41 spread brands and 154 spread names. None of those names describes a portion, a sachet, a pod, or a peel-and-press format. The category has grown, and the format is empty. The charts do not show that a buyer will pay $5.00 NZD for a sheet, and they are not a sales forecast.
50: 
51: ## Competitors
52: 
53: Three jar prices come from New World pages opened on 30 September 2026. The non-Club+ price is the shelf price used here. Each page also showed a lower figure. That figure is recorded and is not treated as the standing price. None of the three is a peel-and-press sheet.
54:

It is peanuts and salt, opened and knifed. The page is https://www.newworld.co.nz/shop/product/5267959_ea_000nw?name=fix--fogg-smooth-peanut-butter
56: 
57: Pic's Smooth Peanut Butter is a 380 g jar. The non-Club+ price was $7.79 NZD, stated as $2.05 NZD per 100 g. The page also showed $6.79 NZD. The wording on the page tells the buyer to take a sturdy table knife and stir, because the oil rises and the salt sinks. The page is https://www.newworld.co.nz/shop/product/5019876_ea_000nw?name=pic%27s-smooth-peanut-butter
58:

It is a hazelnut and cocoa spread for toast, and it still needs a knife and an open tub. The page is https://www.newworld.co.nz/shop/product/5001098_ea_000nw?name=nutella-hazelnut-spread

items.content: Focus is on formulating an effective prompt for the music generation feature. Understanding the optimal input structure is key to achieving desired outputs. The prompt needs to specify genre, mood, tempo, vocal style, and duration.

Here is a tailored prompt designed for **Gemini / Lyria** (under Gemini Tools → Audio/Music generation) to produce a 15–30 second podcast advertisement jingle that aligns with the Stamp brand identity and course marking criteria:

---

### Primary Prompt for Gemini / Lyria

```text
Create a short, catchy 20-second podcast advertisement jingle for a breakfast product called "Stamp". 

Genre & Style: Upbeat indie-pop, warm acoustic guitar, punchy handclaps, bouncy bass, bright and friendly vocal (female or male), clean modern radio production, tempo around 115 BPM.

Duration: 20 seconds.

Lyrics:
[Intro - upbeat acoustic strum & claps] (3s)

[Verse] (7s)
No knife, no dirty jar in sight,
Just peel the sheet and press it right.

[Chorus / Hook] (7s)
Peel, press, hot toast done,
Stamp makes breakfast number one!

[Outro] (3s)
Stamp. Just peel and press.
```

---

### Alternative: Fast & Playful Rhythm Hook

If you prefer a punchier, slightly more energetic vibe (great for short podcast prerolls):

```text
Create a punchy 15-second commercial jingle for "Stamp" toast spread portions.

Genre & Style: Fast, bouncy modern acoustic pop, rhythmic beat, playful delivery, crisp and articulate vocals, tempo around 125 BPM.

Duration: 15 to 20 seconds.

Lyrics:
[Verse]
Forget the knife, forget the mess,
Hot toast ready in a single press!

[Hook]
Peel it, press it, grab and go,
Stamp is the tastiest spread you know!
Stamp!
```

---

### Tips for Gemini / Lyria & Submission:
1. **Pacing and Timing**: Generative music models can sometimes overrun requested durations. Aim for a generation between 15 and 30 seconds. If Gemini outputs a 45-second track, that is still well within the marking guide's strict 15–60 second window.
2. **Saving the File**: Download the generated audio as `.mp3` and save it directly as:
   `audio/stamp-jingle.mp3`
   (If it downloads as `.wav` or `.m4a`, we can convert and trim it with `ffmpeg` in one command).
3. **Chat URL**: Don't forget to use Gemini's **Share** button on that chat session so you can log the shared URL for your chat session submission form.

## 1. What the prior attempt got wrong
1. **`.env` variables not loaded into SvelteKit `process.env`:**
   - **Input:** Providing `OPENROUTER_API_KEY=xyz` in `website/.env` and starting the dev server or build.
   - **Expected:** `GET /api/chat` detects the key and returns `{"openrouterConfigured": true}`.
   - **Actual:** `GET /api/chat` returned `{"openrouterConfigured": false}`.
   - **Root cause:** In SvelteKit, Vite loads `.env` files into its internal env store but does NOT mutate Node's `process.env` for non-`VITE_` prefixed variables. `openrouter.ts` only inspected `process.env['OPENROUTER_API_KEY']`, leaving it empty unless passed directly via the command line.
2. **Brittle refusal regex in `/api/chat`:**
   - **Input:** OpenRouter LLM output saying "Stamp makes no therapeutic claims and cannot cure stomach ulcers. Consult a physician."
   - **Expected:** Flagged with `isRefusal: true` and appropriate `topicTitle` to trigger the red compliance pill/border.
   - **Actual:** `isRefusal` remained `false` because only 4 rigid substring checks were used (`not a medical`, `do not provide health advice`, `does not make organic`, `not gluten-free`).
   - **Root cause:** Hardcoded literal substring matching failed on natural LLM phrasing variations (e.g. "no therapeutic claims", "consult a physician", "does not claim to be organic").
3. **Incomplete verification suite:**
   - **Input:** Running `node website/test-chat.mjs`.
   - **Expected:** Testing the OpenRouter integration module, configuration loader, fallback mechanics, and refusal detection.
   - **Actual:** `test-chat.mjs` only tested `matchQuestion` in `knowledge.ts`, with zero coverage of `openrouter.ts`.

- [website/src/lib/server/openrouter.ts](file:///home/jacob/Documents/INFO123%20Project/website/src/lib/server/openrouter.ts): Added surrounding quote stripping in `getOpenRouterConfig()` to safely handle quoted `.env` values (e.g. `OPENROUTER_API_KEY="sk-..."`).
- [website/src/routes/api/chat/+server.ts](file:///home/jacob/Documents/INFO123%20Project/website/src/routes/api/chat/+server.ts): Broadened refusal detection regex to encompass FSANZ-mandated therapeutic/medical disclaimers and dietary/certification claim refusals, and added descriptive `topicTitle` ('Medical & Therapeutic Refusal' or 'Dietary & Certification Refusal') for OpenRouter responses.

- [presentation/build_deck.py](file:///home/jacob/Documents/INFO123%20Project/presentation/build_deck.py) & [presentation/Stamp-pitch.pptx](file:///home/jacob/Documents/INFO123%20Project/presentation/Stamp-pitch.pptx): Verified and rebuilt the 16:9 widescreen slide deck.

- **Unverified aspects:**

## 4. Known Issues

## 5. Remaining risk & next step

### Phase Completion Update: Website, OpenRouter Chatbot, Pitch Deck & Git Initialized

We have reached a major milestone in the project: **Stages 6, 7, and 9 are now fully implemented and verified**, and the workspace is version-controlled and build-ready.

---

### What Has Been Completed

1. **Business Plan PDF (All 13 Tasks Satisfied)**
   - Updated [business-plan/copy.md](file:///home/jacob/Documents/INFO123%20Project/business-plan/copy.md) to integrate the Customer Support Chatbot (Task 11) and Website Demo (Task 12), ensuring complete coverage of all 13 tasks from the marking guide.
   - Recompiled [business-plan/Stamp-business-plan.pdf](file:///home/jacob/Documents/INFO123%20Project/business-plan/Stamp-business-plan.pdf). Total prose count is exactly **2,456 words** (within the 1,500–2,500 word requirement) across 11 pages with all 6 required visual figures and diagrams embedded.

2. **SvelteKit Website & OpenRouter Chatbot**
   - The Vite development server is live and running at **[http://localhost:5173/](http://localhost:5173/)**.
   - **`/` (Landing Page)**: Showcases the 3-step "Peel. Press. Toast." mechanism, the four launch flavours, pack photography, and pricing ($5.00/sheet, $6.25/100 g).
   - **`/flavours`**: Detailed cards for Salted Butter, Raspberry, Yeast extract, Peanut, and the Mixed Sheet with full ingredient listings, FSANZ allergen declarations, and shelf-stability facts.
   - **`/chat` & `/api/chat` (OpenRouter Integration)**: Built with dual-engine capability. It connects to OpenRouter via `/api/chat` using your configured model (defaulting to `openai/gpt-4o-mini`). When no API key is supplied or if network issues occur, it automatically falls back to our local deterministic knowledge engine without breaking the UI. Strict refusal guardrails were verified against medical advice and unsupported certification claims.
   - Tested: `npm run check` passed with 0 errors, and `npm run build` completed cleanly using `@sveltejs/adapter-vercel`.

3. **Presentation & Video Pitch Package**
   - Built [presentation/Stamp-pitch.pptx](file:///home/jacob/Documents/INFO123%20Project/presentation/Stamp-pitch.pptx) in native 16:9 widescreen format, featuring brand palette styling, wordmark art, pack renders, and market data slides.
   - Authored [presentation/timing.md](file:///home/jacob/Documents/INFO123%20Project/presentation/timing.md):
     - **Part 1 (Investor Pitch)**: A 132-word script designed for a 52–56 second spoken delivery (comfortably under the strict 60-second limit).
     - **Part 2 (Personal Reflection)**: Structured talking points and prompts for Reflection Question 1 (workflow lessons and context rot management) and Question 2 (authenticity, ethics, and combating AI slop), keeping your overall video under the strict 3m29s cutoff.

4. **Git Repository Setup**
   - Initialized Git on the `main` branch with a root [.gitignore](file:///home/jacob/Documents/INFO123%20Project/.gitignore) safeguarding dependencies, caches, and `.env` files.
   - Created the initial commit with all 108 project files staged.

---

### Directions & Decisions for Next Steps

To keep you in control of the next actions, here are the three items ready for your input:

1. **OpenRouter API Key**: 
   When you are ready to test live streaming LLM responses in `/chat`, would you like to provide the key now to add to `website/.env`, or keep using the deterministic fallback for local review?
2. **Vercel Remote & Deployment**:

3. **Lyria Jingle Update**: 
   Once you generate your preferred audio track in Gemini/Lyria using the prompt provided earlier, simply save it to `audio/stamp-jingle.mp3` (or send it over), and we will verify the duration and link it for submission.

Markdown rendering is now active within the chat interface, enabling formatting for lists, emphasis, and code snippets. Simultaneously, all technical identifiers and labels have been removed from the display, leading to a more streamlined and concise presentation. The header has been simplified to "Stamp Support".

The website and chat experience have been updated to support markdown, remove all technical labelling, and provide full mobile responsiveness.

---

### What Was Updated

1. **Markdown Formatting in Chat**
   - Integrated `marked` with GitHub Flavored Markdown (GFM) and automatic line breaks.
   - Formats numbered steps, bulleted lists, bold text, italics, and inline code smoothly inside message bubbles.

2. **Removed Technical Labelling**
   - **Header**: Stripped out raw model names (`nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b:free`), "Spec Knowledge Engine", and internal status tags. The header now displays a clean, consumer-facing **"Stamp Support"** with an **"Online · Ready to help"** status.
   - **Message Bubbles**: Removed all internal topic tags (e.g. `OpenRouter · ...`, `Medical & Therapeutic Refusal`) and source badges (`OpenRouter`, `Verified Spec`). All answers render as clean, friendly brand messages with clean timestamps.

3. **Complete Mobile Optimization**
   - **Chatbot Window**: On mobile screens (`≤ 640px`), the chat drawer opens into a touch-friendly full-screen view with safe-area inset padding (`env(safe-area-inset-top)` and `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)`) so input boxes and headers aren't obscured by mobile navigation bars or gestures. Tap targets (chips, buttons, inputs) meet standard 44px+ mobile touch guidelines.
   - **Landing Page (`/`)**: Hero action buttons stack vertically on small screens, pack imagery scales proportionally, and the 3-step guide and market analysis cards wrap cleanly without horizontal scroll.
   - **Flavours Page (`/flavours`)**: Pack cards, ingredient listings, and allergen declaration tables adapt to a single-column layout with comfortable padding on phones.
   - **Header & Footer**: Mobile-friendly navigation with compact brand logo and stacked footer columns.

---

### Live Verification

You can test these changes live at **[http://localhost:5173/](http://localhost:5173/)** (or on your phone via your local network at `http://192.168.1.22:5173/`).

All changes have passed `svelte-check` (0 errors, 0 warnings), verified production build (`npm run build`), and are committed to Git.

items.content:
Initial color scheme proposed, outlining primary and section-specific palettes for the architecture. Each section will be visually distinct, using a pair of colors for contrast and emphasis: a bright neon tone paired with a deeper, more muted shade.


Defined specific color palettes for the different sections, ensuring strong visual contrast and consistency within each.  The hero section will utilize a purple gradient and electric purple for impactful typography. The peel effect in the hero section relies on scroll-triggered transformations to simulate a sticker peeling, using perspective and rotation to reveal a metallic texture beneath.


Now focusing on the "Explosion Effect" for the 3-step section, triggered by scroll progress to create a dynamic visual of the toast spread discs. items.content: The design update prioritizes a high-brand-presence aesthetic. This involves eliminating white and black from the website's visual elements, including typography, borders, backgrounds, shadows, and the floating chat widget. Instead, the design strictly utilizes brand color pairs such as deep brand purple, electric neon purple, butter gold/caramel, and wild raspberry to achieve a cohesive and authentic visual identity.

The website has been redesigned to deliver a bold brand presence built around the product identity.

---

### What Was Built

1. **Zero White & Zero Black — Pure Brand Palettes**:
   - Replaced all white and black surfaces across the entire site and floating chat widget with the brand color pairs:
     - **House Stamp**: Electric Neon Magenta-Purple (`#E24BFF`) & Deep Night Ink (`#3B0764` / `#240340`).
     - **Salted Butter**: Electric Butter Gold (`#FFD640`) & Roasted Caramel Brown (`#4A3000`).
     - **Raspberry**: Saturated Neon Raspberry (`#FF467A`) & Dark Wild Berry Maroon (`#460820`).
     - **Yeast Extract**: Ultra-Bright Violet (`#E24BFF`) & Deep Ink Purple (`#3B0764`).
     - **Roasted Peanut**: Roasted Peanut Ochre (`#FF8C30`) & Deep Peanut Umber (`#4E2408`).

2. **Full-Screen Hero with Scroll Peel Effect**:
   - Built an interactive full-screen hero section. As you scroll, the top card curls and peels backwards in 3D (`perspective(1400px)` with dynamic rotational tilt and peel drop-shadows), exposing the silver/purple release film backing underneath, mimicking peeling a Stamp spread portion off release film.

3. **Exploding 3-Step Section**:
   - The second full-screen section breaks down the 3-second gesture: **01. PEEL**, **02. PRESS**, and **03. TOAST**.
   - As you scroll past this section, the three cards explode outward in opposite directions (Step 1 blasts top-left with angular rotation, Step 2 accelerates downwards, Step 3 bursts top-right), clearing the screen for the flavour worlds.

4. **Dedicated Full-Screen Flavour Worlds**:
   - Each flavour has its own full-screen, high-contrast visual world:
     - **Salted Butter**: Golden yellow backdrop, 78 g butterfat / 2 g salt specs, and dairy allergen callout.
     - **Slow-Cooked Raspberry**: Neon raspberry backdrop, 150 g fruit / 100 g reduction ratio, and lemon juice preservation facts.
     - **Yeast Extract**: Vivid violet backdrop, 80% yeast extract / 15.5% barley malt formulation, and gluten disclaimer.
     - **Roasted Peanut**: Warm ochre backdrop, 96% peanut purity, and anti-oil separation science.
   - **Interactive Pack Flipper**: Every flavour section features an interactive **"⇄ View Back Ingredients / Front Pack"** toggle to view the real front packaging and nutritional panels.

5. **The Mixed Sheet & Direct Chat Integration**:
   - Concludes with the hero 4-flavour mixed sheet section displaying all 4 packs together, the $5.00 NZD sheet pricing, and one-touch buttons to open the Nemotron support bot.

---

### Try It Live

The dev server is updated and running:
👉 **[http://localhost:5173/](http://localhost:5173/)** (or on mobile at `http://192.168.1.22:5173/`).

Scroll down to see the hero peel away, the 3 steps blast apart, and the full-screen flavour sections take over the screen. All code is verified with zero errors and committed to Git!

The explode animation should be done on a threshold rather than as the user scrolls past, and the header needs to be redesigned to be floating, and follow the color scheme of whatever it is above rather than bneing purple all the time.

Initial hypothesis: implement a 3D card flip animation for ingredient view toggling. This involves a lift effect and then a 180-degree rotation. The "lift" can be achieved with `translateZ` or `scale` transformations. `transform-style: preserve-3d` is required for the 3D effect. A transition will control the animation timing.


The 3D card flip needs refinement; a page-flip animation is more appropriate for the hero section, resembling an e-reader. The page flip will use a spine-based origin with a `rotateY` transformation and a high `perspective` value to sweep the content. The brand's wordmark, located within the `brand/` directory, requires investigation to determine if an SVG or PNG is preferred. The brand style dictates a flat design, eliminating all shadow or glow effects.


An explosion animation, triggered by scroll position, requires a clear threshold for a decisive visual effect. This avoids continuous scrubbing and ensures a clean transition to the exploded state using either CSS transitions or keyframes upon crossing the threshold. The header necessitates a floating design that dynamically adapts its color scheme to the section currently above it. Color mapping to hero sections dictates precise background, text, and border styles.

The header's current CSS indicates a fixed position. The requirement is for it to float and adapt its color. Examining the layout file will help understand how to implement the desired floating behavior and dynamic color scheme based on the content beneath.


Examining the CSS, the current style has the required base styling, and dynamic theme colors are defined. The next step is determining how to trigger the floating behavior based on scrolling and apply the appropriate theme.

Considering the page-flip animation, the primary challenge is achieving a realistic page curl effect during the hero section's initial reveal. The transformation origin must be set to the left edge, and a perspective transform will simulate depth as the "page" rotates. The explode animation requires a threshold trigger, moving away from a scroll-based trigger. An IntersectionObserver or a similar mechanism will detect when the steps section enters the viewport, triggering the animation based on this threshold.


A threshold trigger activates the "explode" animation, setting a flag to true, initiating CSS transitions for each "step".  User control will be added for re-triggering the animation or resetting the state.

items.content:
Reviewing the feature requirements, the `Wordmark` component needs integration within the Hero section, styled with a specific class and color. The e-reader page-flip animation demands establishing a left-spine transform origin and perspective to simulate the page turn based on scroll position. The scrollY threshold will control the animation progression.


The page-flip effect relies on a perspective transformation and rotation controlled by scroll position, with opacity adjusted to simulate the curl. An explosion animation will trigger based on a scroll threshold or an observer, causing cards to translate, rotate, and fade out. Transitions will be employed to give the explosion a kinetic feel.


The page-flip animation's CSS utilizes perspective and `transform-style: preserve-3d` for the 3D effect. The `flipped` class then triggers the rotation. Ensuring the design is strictly flat, all shadows and glowing effects are explicitly excluded from the implementation, focusing on solid fills and sharp borders. The header will use an observer to inherit the color scheme from the content it is above.

The only remaining item is the Jingle; an instrumental version is available, and a prompt for a vocal lyrics version has been provided to the user for external generation.

### Project Status Update

All requested brand refinements have been built, verified, and committed to `main` ([commit 92fc469](file:///home/jacob/Documents/INFO123%20Project)):

1. **Pure Flat Brand Identity (Zero Black or White)**: All glow effects, drop shadows, and text shadows have been removed across the entire site and chat widget in favor of sharp 2–3px flat borders and saturated two-tone brand color blocking. Each flavor section is bathed strictly in its own signature hues—Electric Butter Gold & Roasted Caramel for Butter, Neon Wild Raspberry & Maroon for Raspberry, Electric Violet & Deep Night Ink for Yeast, and Roasted Ochre & Deep Umber for Peanut.
2. **Interactive Motion & Physicality**: The hero now features an **e-reader page-flip animation** that curls along the left spine on scroll to reveal the gesture stage beneath. The **3-Step "Peel, Press, Spread" sequence triggers an explosion on a discrete scroll threshold** with an interactive manual toggle. Each flavor pack card features a **3D lift & flip animation** that lifts 18px and rotates 180° to display the regulatory nutrition panel and ingredients.
3. **Floating Adaptive Wordmark Header & Live Chat**: The floating pill header now incorporates the authentic vector [wordmark.svg](file:///home/jacob/Documents/INFO123%20Project/brand/wordmark.svg) via [`Wordmark.svelte`](file:///home/jacob/Documents/INFO123%20Project/website/src/lib/Wordmark.svelte) and dynamically synchronizes its background, text, and button fills with whichever color section it is currently passing over. The corner chatbot widget ([`ChatWidget.svelte`](file:///home/jacob/Documents/INFO123%20Project/website/src/lib/ChatWidget.svelte)) is live on `http://localhost:5173/` running OpenRouter's `nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b:free` with full markdown support, mobile drawer optimization, and zero technical labels.

---

### Suggested Next Decisions

How would you like to proceed?
- **Option 1: Live UI Check**: You can preview the website directly at **`http://localhost:5173/`** to test the page flip, explosion threshold, 3D card flips, and the dynamic header. Let me know if any timings or color contrasts need tweaking.
- **Option 2: Jingle Integration**: If you have generated the vocal Lyria version of the jingle, you can drop it into [`audio/stamp-jingle.mp3`](file:///home/jacob/Documents/INFO123%20Project/audio/stamp-jingle.mp3) and I will verify its audio duration (15–60s) and wire it into the website demo.
- **Option 3: Vercel Deployment (Stage 8)**: If you're happy with the website, we can link your GitHub repository and deploy the project live to Vercel with your OpenRouter API key configured.

Scroll events are used to update the peel progress based on the element's position relative to the viewport. The progress is mapped to a specific range representing the peel's open state.


The manual toggle function directly manipulates the `peelProgress` variable and updates the animation state through the instance, allowing the UI to control the peel effect. HTML structure defines the visual presentation, including elements for the "peel" animation, beneath layer content, and manual control interaction. The `bind:this` directive establishes the element references for JavaScript interaction.


The HTML structure outlines a visual design with distinct layers for a "peel" animation effect. The back layer includes a foil pattern, while the top layer encompasses text, imagery, and interactive elements. Interaction is controlled through a manual toggle function and key press, allowing control over the "peel" progress.


The HTML structure suggests a layered "peel" animation implemented using CSS. Specific classes identify the different layers: `.peel-bottom`, `.peel-back`, and `.peel-top`. CSS styling positions elements absolutely and sets `transform-origin` for the layer animation. The `.hero-peel-track`, `.hero-peel-sticky` and `.hero-peel-box` have additional styles to handle scrolling and viewport positioning.


The button's HTML structure indicates a state change controlled by a `flipped` variable, which toggles on click, using an SVG icon and text. The analysis suggests integrating the visual effects into a transition upon the state change.


The button's state change is visually animated with a pulse effect via CSS animation and transforms on hover and active states. The background transition utilizes a timing function to create a smooth color change. The floating header's appearance is dynamically updated in sync with the section's background. Each section's transparent background creates the illusion of a stationary background with a fading color effect.

The analysis is now focused on color style verification within the main page to ensure no white text elements exist. Reviewed color assignments across multiple sections, confirming no white text appears in any of the targeted elements.


Color assignments are being examined for different UI components, specifically focusing on the "butter" and "raspberry" flavors. Color schemes for "yeast" and "peanut" flavors are being analyzed to ensure consistent application across all UI components. Each component's color associations are recorded to verify intended contrast and branding. The mixed section’s distinct styling also needs verification.

items.content:
### Progress Update: Peel Animation, Stationary Morphing Canvas & Animated Flip Triggers

All four adjustments have been implemented, verified, and committed to `main` ([commit 52322fc](file:///home/jacob/Documents/INFO123%20Project)):

1. **Physical Peel Animation with `peel.js`**: We replaced the 3D book rotation with **`peel.js`** in the Hero section ([`+page.svelte`](file:///home/jacob/Documents/INFO123%20Project/website/src/routes/+page.svelte)). The Hero sheet now behaves like an authentic sticker disc: as you scroll, the bottom-right corner peels back diagonally across the screen via SVG clip-paths, rolling over a patterned brand foil back to reveal the hot sourdough and 10 g spread disc underneath. It also supports interactive mouse/touch dragging directly on the corner and a quick corner toggle button. In accordance with the flat branding rule, all drop shadows, box shadows, and specular reflections remain disabled (`topShadow: false`, `backShadow: false`, `backReflection: false`).
2. **Stationary Viewport Background with Seamless Color Fading**: Rather than scrolling past individual colored blocks, the canvas background is now **completely stationary** across the entire viewport (`position: fixed; inset: 0;`). As you scroll through the page, the stationary background smoothly fades between the signature brand colors at each section's midpoint threshold: Deep Night Ink (`#240340`) for Hero & 3 Steps → Electric Butter Gold (`#ffd640`) → Neon Wild Raspberry (`#ff467a`) → Electric Violet (`#e24bff`) → Roasted Peanut Ochre (`#ff8c30`) → Deep Night Ink (`#240340`) for the Mixed Pack and Footer. The floating header dynamically harmonizes with this transition.
3. **Animated Lift & Flip Triggers & Zero White Text**: The **Lift & Flip buttons** on each flavour card have been animated with an ambient subtle tactile pulse (`@keyframes flipButtonPulse`), dual-curved SVG rotating arrows that spin 180°–360° on hover and flip, an active press downstate, and interactive pill badges (`[3D LIFT]` / `[BACK PANEL]`). Additionally, all instances of white text and white box backgrounds across the flavour worlds, spec cards, callout alerts, and nutritional panels have been purged and replaced strictly with the contrasting saturated brand color pairs (e.g. Dark Maroon `#460820` for Raspberry, Deep Ink `#3b0764` for Yeast, Roasted Umber `#4e2408` for Peanut, and Caramel Brown `#4a3000` for Butter).

---

### Preview & Direction

The Vite dev server is running live on **`http://localhost:5173/`**:
- **Test the Peel**: Scroll down from the top or grab the bottom-right corner to peel back the hero sheet.
- **Watch the Background Fade**: Scroll continuously through the flavours to experience the stationary viewport canvas fading between the brand colors.
- **Try the Flip Buttons**: Hover over and click any of the "Lift & Flip" buttons to inspect the animated rotation and card flip.

Does this feel like the right peeling feel and background presence, or would you like to adjust any of the peel curves, scroll speeds, or button timings?

The user explicitly requests the removal of the peel animation from the hero section. The aim is to replace it with a clean and conventional header presentation. Understanding what constitutes a "nice, clean, normal header" is crucial to correctly implement the change.


The focus shifts to the hero section's visual elements, transitioning from the dynamic peel effect to a static presentation. This involves integrating the wordmark, tagline, product image, value proposition, key facts, and call-to-action buttons. A key aspect is eliminating the prominent border outlines, echoing the user's preference for flat color blocking and clean geometric designs, especially for the header bar.

items.content:
The CSS defines a `floating-header` class with fixed positioning, centered horizontally, and styled with a border and rounded corners. Examining the Svelte code, the `<header>` element applies this `floating-header` class along with `site-header` and sets the `background-color` based on `currentTheme`. This implies the header's appearance and positioning are controlled through these styles.


The CSS border on the header and button needs removal, changing them to flat color blocks to match the flavors section.  The `border` property can be set to `none`, the `border-color` attribute is unnecessary, and rounded corners can be implemented to achieve a pill shape.  I should update the theme configuration file, removing the need for `border` styling.  The color values for the header background, text, button background, and button text will be used to ensure correct theming.


Examining the theme configurations reveals a pattern of header and button styling directly linked to the screen background, with no outline borders defined. It should be possible to remove any explicit border styles and rely solely on the background color for visual separation. Removing the animation requirement simplifies header implementation and aligns perfectly with existing theme-based styling.


Initial focus is on removing the existing "peel" interaction and replacing it with a standard Hero section.  This requires modifying the Svelte component. items.content:
### Update: Clean Hero & Full Removal of Outline Borders

The peel animation has been removed and the site has been redesigned to use pure flat color blocking without wireframe outline borders ([commit 816e302](file:///home/jacob/Documents/INFO123%20Project)):

1. **Clean, Normal, High-Impact Hero**: We eliminated the complex peel scroll track, sticky wrappers, and clipping paths. In its place is a clean, normal, full-screen Hero section ([`+page.svelte`](file:///home/jacob/Documents/INFO123%20Project/website/src/routes/+page.svelte)) showcasing the authentic vector [`Wordmark.svelte`](file:///home/jacob/Documents/INFO123%20Project/website/src/lib/Wordmark.svelte), the bold `PEEL. PRESS. TOAST.` tagline, the 8-stamp card packshot, key value points ($5.00 NZD / sheet, 8 × 10 g discs, 12-month ambient pantry stability), and smooth call-to-action buttons (`Explore The 4 Flavours ↓` and `How Stamp Works ↓`).
2. **Flat Solid Header Bar (Zero Outlines)**: The floating header bar ([`+layout.svelte`](file:///home/jacob/Documents/INFO123%20Project/website/src/routes/+layout.svelte)) is now a **completely borderless flat pill**. As it floats above the stationary color-morphing background, it displays a solid flat fill matching the active flavor world (e.g. Deep Night Ink `#3b0764` over Butter Gold, Berry Maroon `#460820` over Raspberry, Deep Ink `#3b0764` over Yeast, and Deep Peanut Umber `#4e2408` over Peanut Ochre) with zero outline strokes, matching the flat aesthetic of the flavors section.
3. **Pure Flat Color Blocking Across All Sections**: All remaining outline borders (`border: 2px solid`, `border: 3px solid`, border-tops) have been removed across the 3 Step cards, flavor spec blocks, callout containers, pricing cards, and chat widget. Every element now sits as a solid flat shape with rich color contrast and zero white or black, maintaining the animated 3D lift-and-flip card interactions and the stationary viewport background color transitions.

---

### Preview & Direction

The updated interface is live on **`http://localhost:5173/`**. Please take a look at the clean hero, borderless floating header, and flat color-blocked sections. Let me know what you think and what we should work on next!

turns.userPrompt: This is getting much better. We should introduce a rule around the colors, in that there should only ever be 3 colors on screen at a time - primary, secondary, and tertiary and optionally black and white. The hgero is a great example of this where the wordmark is primary, bg secondary, and header bg tertiary. There is only ever to be one colorshceme object, which all elements refer to, so that everything on the page changes color at once.

items.content:
Focusing on the color constraint: the user wants a maximum of three colors (primary, secondary, tertiary), plus optional black and white. The "hgero" example illustrates this principle: wordmark (primary), background (secondary), and header background (tertiary). Ensuring that there is only one "colorshceme object" is essential.


The color constraint necessitates a single, globally accessible color scheme object. This object will define the three core colors (primary, secondary, tertiary) plus optional black and white. The **strict 3-color brand rule** and **single global color scheme object architecture** are fully implemented, verified, and running live on the dev server.

### What Was Implemented:

1. **Single Global `colorScheme` Object ([`theme.svelte.ts`](file:///home/jacob/Documents/INFO123%20Project/website/src/lib/theme.svelte.ts))**:
   - Only **one** reactive `colorScheme` object exists (`$state<ColorScheme>({ primary, secondary, tertiary })`).
   - All elements across the entire website (stationary screen background, floating header, wordmark, navigation, buttons, cards, callouts, and the support chatbot) directly reference this single object or its bound CSS variables (`--color-primary`, `--color-secondary`, `--color-tertiary`).
   - When the user scrolls past each section threshold, `setSectionTheme()` updates `colorScheme.primary`, `colorScheme.secondary`, and `colorScheme.tertiary` synchronously, morphing every on-screen element in unison.

2. **Strict 3-Color Screen Rule**:
   - **Hero Section**:
     - `primary`: `#e24bff` (STAMP Wordmark, primary actions, highlights)
     - `secondary`: `#240340` (Screen background)
     - `tertiary`: `#3b0764` (Floating header background & cards)
   - **Flavour 1 (Salted Butter)**:
     - `primary`: `#ffd640` (Electric Butter Gold)
     - `secondary`: `#4a3000` (Roasted Caramel Brown screen background)
     - `tertiary`: `#2d1d00` (Deep Roast Umber header & cards)
   - **Flavour 2 (Raspberry)**:
     - `primary`: `#ff467a` (Neon Wild Raspberry)
     - `secondary`: `#460820` (Dark Berry Maroon screen background)
     - `tertiary`: `#2d0414` (Deepest Maroon header & cards)
   - **Flavour 3 (Yeast Extract)**:
     - `primary`: `#e24bff` (Electric Violet)
     - `secondary`: `#240340` (Deep Night Ink screen background)
     - `tertiary`: `#18012b` (Deepest Violet header & cards)
   - **Flavour 4 (Roasted Peanut)**:
     - `primary`: `#ff8c30` (Roasted Peanut Ochre)
     - `secondary`: `#4e2408` (Deep Peanut Umber screen background)
     - `tertiary`: `#2d1403` (Dark Roast Peanut header & cards)
   - High-contrast pure white is used strictly for body paragraph readability.

3. **100% Flat Brand Aesthetic**:
   - Removed all wireframe borders (`border: 2px solid`, `border: 3px solid`) from the floating header pill, step cards, flavour cards, spec boxes, and chat modal.
   - The UI is composed purely of clean, flat, bold color blocks.

4. **Floating Dynamic Header & Hero**:
   - The header floats with tertiary background, primary wordmark/nav links, and primary CTA button.
   - Clean, high-impact hero featuring the authentic drawn vector STAMP wordmark.

items.content:
The background colors for the flavour sections have been restored to their bright, punchy brand colors as before, while preserving the strict **3-color rule** and the **single global `colorScheme` object architecture**:

### Updated Color Scheme Palettes ([`theme.svelte.ts`](file:///home/jacob/Documents/INFO123%20Project/website/src/lib/theme.svelte.ts))

- **Hero & 3 Steps**:
  - `primary`: `#e24bff` (Drawn vector STAMP wordmark, actions, highlights)
  - `secondary`: `#240340` (Deep Night Ink background)
  - `tertiary`: `#3b0764` (Floating header background, cards)
- **Flavour 1: Salted Butter**:
  - `secondary`: `#ffd640` (**Bright Electric Butter Gold screen background**)
  - `tertiary`: `#4a3000` (Roasted Caramel Brown header background, card surfaces, and bold headlines)
  - `primary`: `#ffd640` (Electric Gold wordmark in floating header, button text, spec kickers)
- **Flavour 2: Slow-Cooked Raspberry**:
  - `secondary`: `#ff467a` (**Bright Neon Wild Raspberry screen background**)
  - `tertiary`: `#460820` (Dark Berry Maroon header background, card surfaces, and bold headlines)
  - `primary`: `#ff467a` (Neon Raspberry wordmark in floating header, button text, spec kickers)
- **Flavour 3: Yeast Extract**:
  - `secondary`: `#e24bff` (**Bright Electric Violet screen background**)
  - `tertiary`: `#240340` (Deep Night Ink header background, card surfaces, and bold headlines)
  - `primary`: `#e24bff` (Electric Violet wordmark in floating header, button text, spec kickers)
- **Flavour 4: Roasted Peanut**:
  - `secondary`: `#ff8c30` (**Bright Roasted Peanut Ochre screen background**)
  - `tertiary`: `#4e2408` (Deep Peanut Umber header background, card surfaces, and bold headlines)
  - `primary`: `#ff8c30` (Peanut Ochre wordmark in floating header, button text, spec kickers)

### Key Improvements Made:
1. **Bright Backgrounds Restored**: When scrolling down, the screen transitions into bright, saturated yellow, pink, violet, and orange worlds, eliminating the dark/mellow appearance.
2. **High-Contrast Typography**: Headlines, numbers, and lead descriptions on each flavour screen now dynamically use `var(--color-tertiary)` (the rich dark contrast tone), ensuring crisp readability against the bright backgrounds.
3. **Chatbot Contrast Alignment**: Chat modal surfaces, message bubbles, chips, and launcher buttons now pair `primary` with `tertiary` to guarantee clean text contrast regardless of which flavour section is active.

The Vite dev server is running on `http://localhost:5173/`.

items.content:
The hero section has been massively simplified in [`+page.svelte`](file:///home/jacob/Documents/INFO123%20Project/website/src/routes/+page.svelte):

### Changes Applied:
- **Removed Clutter**: Removed the product packshot image, badges row, sub-lead paragraph, and kicker.
- **Ultra-Minimal, High-Impact Content**:
  1. **STAMP Wordmark**: Scaled up to `max-width: 660px; height: 150px` using the drawn authentic vector SVG in `colorScheme.primary`.
  2. **Tagline**: Bold, oversized `PEEL. PRESS. TOAST.` typography.
  3. **Action Buttons**:
     - `Explore The 4 Flavours ↓` (Primary bold flat pill CTA)
     - `How Stamp Works ↓` (Secondary flat pill CTA linking directly to the 3-Step Gesture)
- **Viewport Balance**: Centered vertically in the viewport (`min-height: 100dvh`) with clean spacing (`gap: 2.25rem`).

The dev server is live on `http://localhost:5173/` ready for preview.

turns.userPrompt: Actually, we should add a little more to the hero - that's a little too minimalist at the moment

items.content:
Considering how to enrich the hero design without sacrificing clarity, revisiting past iterations is crucial. Evaluating both options to determine the most effective path forward. The initial preference leans towards a comprehensive layout if that aligns with the implicit product requirements.


Considering the user's feedback, the hero requires additional visual weight to avoid feeling empty, while retaining simplicity. Reviewing prior iterations confirms an initial minimalist design which the user found too sparse, especially with image removal. A key fact strip or the product itself may offer the necessary balance to the brand name and tagline.

The hero section has been re-tuned in [`+page.svelte`](file:///home/jacob/Documents/INFO123%20Project/website/src/routes/+page.svelte) to hit a balanced blend of bold brand minimalism and tangible product richness:

### What Was Added Back:
1. **The Core Pitch (Lead Description)**:
   > *"Single-serve 10 g spread discs on release film. Pressed onto hot toast, it softens into an even layer in seconds — no knife, no messy jar, no wash-up."*
2. **Product Packshot Showcase**:
   - Clean, centered visual presentation of the 8-stamp card sheet ([`pack.png`](file:///home/jacob/Documents/INFO123%20Project/website/static/pack.png)) with a bold flat pill badge (`8 DISCS · 80 g`).

   - `$5.00 NZD / Sheet` · `12-Month Pantry Stable` · `No Jar Waste`
   - Rendered as flat solid pills using `var(--color-tertiary)` and `var(--color-primary)` (zero outline borders).
4. **Primary & Secondary Action CTAs**:
   - `Explore The 4 Flavours ↓`
   - `How Stamp Works ↓`

This gives visitors immediate clarity on what Stamp is and how it looks, while preserving the clean flat design and 3-color palette rules.

Check it out live on `http://localhost:5173/`.

items.content:
Analyzing the CSS rules applied to `.flip-stage`, `.flip-card`, and `.flip-face` elements. The `perspective` property on the stage suggests a 3D transformation context.  The `transform-style: preserve-3d` on the card confirms this, enabling the flipping effect. The `flipped` class's transform properties, including `rotateY(180deg)`, dictate the visual flip animation.


Examining the CSS for `.flip-face`, it seems the packaging is directly represented by the card's SVG, enhanced with a drop shadow for depth. This likely avoids the need for a separate container for the card art. Considering the mixed pack display, the current image could potentially be replaced with an SVG grid for improved visual integration and potentially better responsiveness. Replacing the image with a grid of individual flavor pack components will achieve the desired effect.

items.content:
All three requested improvements are now live:

### 1. Fixed "How Stamp Works" Button Link
- Corrected the target anchor on the 3-step section from `id="steps-section"` to `id="steps"` in [`+page.svelte`](file:///home/jacob/Documents/INFO123%20Project/website/src/routes/+page.svelte#L112).
- Clicking **"How Stamp Works ↓"** from the hero (or navigating to `/#steps`) now scrolls directly to the 3-Step Gesture section.

---

### 2. Converted All Packaging to Pure SVGs That Follow Color Transitions
All raster PNG images have been replaced with dedicated pure vector SVG components:
- **[`FlavourPackFront.svelte`](file:///home/jacob/Documents/INFO123%20Project/website/src/lib/FlavourPackFront.svelte)**:
  - Vector STAMP wordmark at the top.
  - Authentic line drawings (scored butter block, raspberry cluster, dual barley ears, peanut shells) matching the brand icon specification.
  - Bold typography and bottom `PEEL. PRESS. TOAST.` peel bar.
  - Dynamically styled with `fill="var(--color-tertiary)"` for the pack card base and `fill="var(--color-primary)"` / `stroke="var(--color-primary)"` for artwork and typography.
  - **Color Transitions**: As you scroll between flavours, the packaging card itself smoothly transitions its colors in unison with the viewport background and floating header.
- **[`FlavourPackBack.svelte`](file:///home/jacob/Documents/INFO123%20Project/website/src/lib/FlavourPackBack.svelte)**:
  - Vector mini-icon, ingredient runs, bold allergen notices, and calculated nutrition tables.
  - Also dynamically styled with `var(--color-tertiary)` and `var(--color-primary)`.

---

### 3. Removed Secondary Color Container Enclosing the Packs
- Removed `background: var(--color-tertiary)` and inner padding from the `.flip-face` container.
- The packaging card itself is now the standalone object, floating cleanly over the screen background with a natural drop-shadow (`filter: drop-shadow(0 20px 48px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.22))`).
- Clicking **"Lift & Flip: View Back Ingredients"** lifts and rotates the SVG packaging card 180° in 3D to reveal the SVG nutrition and ingredient panel.
- The Mixed Sheet section has also been updated to render a 2×2 grid of the 4 SVG packs instead of a static raster image.

Preview the live updates on `http://localhost:5173/`.

turns.userPrompt: The grid at the bottom needs to still sue the original colors. Also, I want to revers emy decision on the background colors - just noticed that almost all apges only have two colors isntead of using the full 3

items.content:
The user refers to the bottom grid, specifically the 4-pack grid within the Mixed Sheet section. This grid displays four distinct packs: Butter, Raspberry, Yeast, and Peanut. Previously, all four packs were incorrectly using the same CSS variables.


The grid's packs currently display incorrect colors; the user wants each pack in the bottom grid to retain its original flavor-specific color scheme. The initial solution involves updating the component to accept an option for standalone display or original color usage to correctly render the flavor's colors, using a flavor palette constant. The user also reversed the decision about using three colors for backgrounds, noticing most pages use only two.


Analyzing a previous commit, observed that three distinct colors were consistently present: a secondary screen background, a tertiary card/header background, and a primary wordmark/highlight color. This suggests a design rule with three active colors is viable.

Examining color values, confirmed that flavor-specific palettes were correctly implemented in the earlier design, indicating a functional approach. It is worth evaluating the design choice of using 3 colors, versus the user's reversal to 2 colors.


The user's feedback clearly indicates a preference for the original three-color scheme, which provides better visual distinction. Modifying the `secondary` color to match `primary` led to the undesirable two-color appearance, which the user wants to revert. The user explicitly requests returning to the three-color system, defining specific roles for each color (secondary for background, tertiary for cards/headers, primary for highlights).


Reviewing the commit history, identified the original `THEME_PALETTES` defining the flavor-specific color schemes, noting the assignment of primary, secondary, and tertiary colors to different visual elements. This confirms the intended structure. Observed that viewport backgrounds in the page were previously assigned the `secondary` color value, aligning with the initial design.


Analyzing the provided color scheme details, the existing three-color hierarchy seems critical: primary for highlights, secondary for background, and tertiary for surface elements. This contrasts with the two-color approach the user reverted.

The previous commit history and the user's feedback both strongly suggest reverting to the three-color scheme to ensure visual consistency and correct flavor representation in the bottom grid. The goal is to enforce the flavor-specific color schemes as originally designed.


The current implementation uses CSS variables for colors, leading to color conflicts in the mixed pack grid. Determined that `FlavourPackFront` and `FlavourPackBack` components require modification to handle original flavor-specific colors when a standalone display is needed. This will involve introducing a new boolean prop and a color palette constant.

All updates have been implemented and verified:

1. **Mixed Sheet Pack Grid Uses Original Brand Colors**:
   - Both [`FlavourPackFront.svelte`](file:///home/jacob/Documents/INFO123%20Project/website/src/lib/FlavourPackFront.svelte) and [`FlavourPackBack.svelte`](file:///home/jacob/Documents/INFO123%20Project/website/src/lib/FlavourPackBack.svelte) now support the `standalone` prop.
   - In [`+page.svelte`](file:///home/jacob/Documents/INFO123%20Project/website/src/routes/+page.svelte#L484-L487), the Mixed Sheet grid passes `standalone={true}` to all 4 flavour packs (`butter`, `raspberry`, `yeast`, `peanut`), rendering them in their authentic brand hues (Gold, Pink, Violet, Ochre) simultaneously on the Mixed Sheet without inheriting the active section's dynamic palette.

2. **Reverted Background Colors & Restored Full 3-Color Hierarchy**:
   - In [`theme.svelte.ts`](file:///home/jacob/Documents/INFO123%20Project/website/src/lib/theme.svelte.ts#L9-L45), every section now features 3 distinct, harmonious colors on screen at all times:
     - **`primary`** (Electric highlight): Title text, icons, buttons, and wordmark.
     - **`secondary`** (Viewport background): Rich, deep tonal background (`#4a3000` butter caramel, `#460820` berry, `#240340` night ink, `#4e2408` peanut umber).
     - **`tertiary`** (Card/surface elevation): Deep elevated card surfaces and header background (`#2d1d00`, `#2d0414`, `#18012b`, `#2d1403`).
     - **Body copy**: High-contrast `#ffffff` text.

3. **Packaging Assets Are Pure Vector SVGs**:
   - Completely freed from outer background boxes.
   - Smoothly interpolate across color transitions on their dedicated screens while preserving original colors in the Mixed Sheet grid.

Both features are now built and active:

1. **Favicon Added**:

   - Linked in [`app.html`](file:///home/jacob/Documents/INFO123%20Project/website/src/app.html#L7-L8) with modern SVG and fallback PNG headers.

2. **Custom Gooey Morphing Cursor**:
   - Built [`MorphCursor.svelte`](file:///home/jacob/Documents/INFO123%20Project/website/src/lib/MorphCursor.svelte) and mounted it in [`+layout.svelte`](file:///home/jacob/Documents/INFO123%20Project/website/src/routes/+layout.svelte#L18).

items.content:
The cursor mechanics and layering in [`MorphCursor.svelte`](file:///home/jacob/Documents/INFO123%20Project/website/src/lib/MorphCursor.svelte) have been refined:

1. **Eliminated Unwanted Rotation while Morphing**:
   - `rotate(...)` is now disabled as soon as an interactive element is targeted (`{isHovered ? '' : 'rotate(...)'}` and `blobAngle = 0`).
   - In free movement, rotation is strictly gated to intentional velocity (`speed > 2.5px/frame`), eliminating angle jitter and spinning when easing into elements.

2. **Fixed Overlaying on Header and Chat Buttons**:
   - Adjusted the cursor layer's `z-index` to `900`—placing it directly behind the floating header (`z-index: 1000`) and the chat launcher/window (`z-index: 9999`).
   - When hovering over navigation links, the "Ask Stamp" button, or chat triggers, the cursor snaps to the element's position and fades seamlessly into the component's back surface rather than sitting across the text or icons.
   - The hovered components transition their own colors to high-contrast active states (`#ffffff` background for primary buttons, `var(--color-primary)` for tertiary buttons and round flip icons) cleanly without being obscured.

3. **Packaging Cards and Inner Chat Ignored**:
   - Explicitly restricted hover triggers so packaging cards, SVG artworks, chat messages, and input text areas are ignored.

The cursor architecture has been rebuilt into a **true background morph**:

1. **How the True Morph Works**:
   - Rather than floating an overlay on top of buttons and links, the cursor layer sits at `z-index: 10000`.
   - When hovering any interactive element (header links, "Ask Stamp", round flip icon, hero/footer action buttons), the element’s own static background is made transparent (`background-color: transparent !important`), and its text/icons are elevated to `z-index: 10002`.

2. **No Missed Clicks (Proxy Click Delegation)**:
   - When the cursor is snapped into an element, a global click listener immediately triggers `.click()` directly on that hovered element. Clicking anywhere while an element is magnetically morphed is guaranteed to fire the button/link immediately.

3. **Consistent Brand Color Scheme**:
   - The morphed background adopts the active section's palette colors (`var(--color-tertiary)` for primary buttons and `var(--color-primary)` for pills/nav links), never using plain white.
   - Clean, crisp circular dot in free motion with zero stretching distortion or rotation artifacts.

Smooth entrance animations have been added for the chat in [`website/src/lib/ChatWidget.svelte`](file:///home/jacob/Documents/INFO123%20Project/website/src/lib/ChatWidget.svelte):

1. **User Message Bubble**:
   - Anchored to the bottom-right (`transform-origin: bottom right`) with a spring-eased scale (`0.92 → 1`) and slide (`translateY(8px) translateX(6px) → 0`) using `cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.4, 0.64, 1)`.

2. **Assistant Response Bubble**:
   - Anchored to the bottom-left (`transform-origin: bottom left`) with a fluid scale (`0.92 → 1`) and directional glide (`translateY(8px) translateX(-6px) → 0`).

3. **Assistant Avatar (`S` badge)**:
   - Pops in with an elastic overshoot scale (`0.6 → 1`) using `cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1)`.

4. **Message Row Container**:
   - Soft vertical fade-in (`translateY(10px) → 0`, `opacity 0 → 1`) over `0.3s`.

Both `npm run check` and `npm run build` pass with zero errors, and the changes are committed to `main` (`b5ae097`). You can test the interactions live on [http://localhost:5173/](http://localhost:5173/).

The specs page at [`website/src/routes/flavours/+page.svelte`](file:///home/jacob/Documents/INFO123%20Project/website/src/routes/flavours/+page.svelte) has undergone a complete makeover:

### Key Enhancements:
1. **Interactive Flavour Selector**:
   - Modern pill navigation bar with active color dot indicators allows you to instantly switch between **Salted Butter**, **Raspberry**, **Yeast Extract**, and **Roasted Peanut**.
   - Switching flavours dynamically updates the page theme palette (`colorScheme`), smoothly transitioning the background, header, and chat bar to match the active flavour's authentic palette.

2. **Interactive 3D Lift & Flip Pack Inspector**:
   - Displays the vector pack front and back directly on a sticky showcase column.
   - Includes the circular flip action button (`round-flip-btn`) that smoothly rotates the card in 3D perspective to reveal the authentic Nutritional Information Panel (NIP) and ingredients on the back.

3. **High-Density Specification Matrix**:
   - 4-card matrix grid detailing **Taste Profile**, **Industrial Formulation** (ratios, moisture control, zero-added preservatives), **Pack & Portion** ($5.00 NZD, 80 g, 8 × 10 g discs, $6.25 / 100 g, 12 months ambient), and **Allergens & Audited Facility Declarations**.
   - Feature highlight chips for quick scannability.

4. **Full Nutrition Information Panel (NIP)**:
   - Formatted table matching Food Standards Code requirements (average quantity per 10 g serve and per 100 g) with clear saturated fat and sugar breakdowns.

5. **The Mixed Sheet Section**:
   - Dedicated card breaking down the 2× disc distribution across all 4 flavours on a single 8-disc sheet, complete with allergen warnings and price breakout.

6. **Regulatory & Compliance Assurance**:
   - 3-card compliance section reinforcing truth-in-advertising: zero therapeutic claims, accurate gluten/allergen disclosures, and honest "butter spread" standard of identity.

Both `npm run check` and `npm run build` pass cleanly, and the changes are committed to `main` (`b3cdad4`). You can preview the interactive specs page live at [http://localhost:5173/flavours](http://localhost:5173/flavours).

The specs page has been streamlined down to pure technical clarity in [`website/src/routes/flavours/+page.svelte`](file:///home/jacob/Documents/INFO123%20Project/website/src/routes/flavours/+page.svelte):

### What Was Cut & Streamlined:
1. **Zero Repetitive Marketing Fluff**:
   - Removed the long marketing paragraphs, taste profile essays, duplicate pricing banners, and redundant compliance essays that were echoing the homepage.
2. **Compact 4-Tab Switcher**:
   - Simple, elegant tab strip (`Butter`, `Raspberry`, `Yeast`, `Peanut`) with instant theme sync.
3. **Clean Side-by-Side Technical Layout**:
   - **Left**: The interactive vector pack with a simple flip pill (`Show NIP & Back` / `Show Pack Front`).
   - **Right**: Concise, structured data:
     - Clear one-line industrial formulation summary.
     - **Exact Ingredients** list.
     - **Allergen Notice** (highlighting milk, gluten, and peanut declarations).
     - **Shelf Stability** (12-month ambient storage).
     - **Nutrition per 10 g Disc**: A clean horizontal 7-cell metric row showing Energy, Fat, Saturated Fat, Carbohydrates, Sugars, Protein, and Sodium at a glance.
     - One discrete footnote noting Mixed Sheet availability and Food Standards Code compliance.

Typecheck and build both passed with 0 errors/warnings, and the change is committed to `main` (`5c17a37`). You can review it live at [http://localhost:5173/flavours](http://localhost:5173/flavours).

items.content:
All four adjustments have been implemented:

1. **Header Spacing**:
   - Increased the top padding on the specs page (`.specs-page`) from `6rem` to `8.5rem`, providing generous breathing room below the fixed floating header before the `SPECIFICATIONS` title.

2. **Circular Icon Flip Button**:
   - Replaced the wide pill button with the round floating icon button (`.round-flip-btn`) matching the main page. It features the rotational arrow SVG that smoothly rotates 180° when flipped.

3. **Removed Mixed Sheet Row**:
   - The Mixed Sheet callout at the bottom of the data column has been removed, keeping the page strictly focused on the selected flavour's technical and nutritional parameters.

4. **Footer Color Scheme Reactivity**:
   - In [`website/src/routes/+layout.svelte`](file:///home/jacob/Documents/INFO123%20Project/website/src/routes/+layout.svelte), replaced the hardcoded purple colors (`#f4c7ff`, `#d896ff`, `#b56be8`) with dynamic variables (`var(--color-primary)` for headings, tagline, and bottom copyright, with clean opacity-tinted white for body copy and links).
   - The footer now transitions smoothly to match whichever flavour theme is currently active (Butter Gold, Raspberry Pink, Yeast Violet, or Peanut Ochre).

Both `npm run check` and `npm run build` pass with zero errors, and the commit (`be82898`) is live on the dev server at [http://localhost:5173/flavours](http://localhost:5173/flavours).
