items.content:
The specifications page has been polished for mobile devices in [`website/src/routes/flavours/+page.svelte`](file:///home/jacob/Documents/INFO123%20Project/website/src/routes/flavours/+page.svelte):

### Mobile Enhancements:
1. **Flavour Tabs**:
   - Organized into an equal 4-column grid (`display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(4, 1fr)`) with a maximum width of `360px`.
   - Balanced padding and font sizes so all four buttons fit without awkward wrapping or horizontal scrolling.
2. **Pack Presentation & Controls**:
   - The pack stage scales proportionally to `270px × 360px`, maintaining crisp SVG clarity and proper 3D flip card perspective.
   - The circular flip icon button is sized down to `48px` for comfortable thumb tap targets.
3. **Typography & Spacing**:
   - Title scaled to `2.1rem` with `5.5rem` top padding to leave comfortable clearance beneath the floating header on smaller screens.
   - Flavour titles and formulation lines scaled down for readability on narrow phone viewports.
4. **Technical Grid & Nutrition Panel**:
   - 2×2 technical parameters card stack seamlessly into a single column.
   - The 7-cell NIP metric row switches to an auto-fit grid (`minmax(68px, 1fr)`) that adjusts neatly across any phone screen width without cutting off or overlapping text.
   - Bottom padding set to `6rem` so the fixed bottom chat bar never obscures any content.

Both `npm run check` and `npm run build` pass with zero errors, and the commit (`f442a03`) is live on the dev server at [http://localhost:5173/flavours](http://localhost:5173/flavours).

 1 file changed, 7 insertions(+), 8 deletions(-)

items.content:
The root cause was that `.pack-card` uses `height: 100%`, which collapsed inside an `aspect-ratio`-based container when no fixed height was present on the stage.

### The Fix in [`website/src/routes/flavours/+page.svelte`](file:///home/jacob/Documents/INFO123%20Project/website/src/routes/flavours/+page.svelte):
1. **Explicit Heights**:
   - Replaced `aspect-ratio` with `max-width: 300px; height: 400px` on mobile (`max-width: 340px; height: 450px` on desktop/tablet).
   - This ensures the 3D perspective stage, front face, and back nutrition panel have a full, robust bounding box, matching the large, crisp presentation seen on the homepage.
2. **Pack Panel Width**:
   - Added `width: 100%` to `.pack-panel` to ensure full centering without parent container shrinkage.

Both `npm run check` and `npm run build` pass with zero errors, and the fix (`47112fc`) is live on the dev server at [http://localhost:5173/flavours](http://localhost:5173/flavours).

items.content:
Yes, **Vercel will work perfectly**, and **your OpenRouter API key will NOT be exposed to the browser/client**, even without a separate backend server.

---

### Why OpenRouter Key is Safe on Vercel:

1. **SvelteKit Serverless Endpoints (`+server.ts`)**:
   - The chatbot's logic is implemented in [`website/src/routes/api/chat/+server.ts`](file:///home/jacob/Documents/INFO123%20Project/website/src/routes/api/chat/+server.ts).
   - In SvelteKit with `@sveltejs/adapter-vercel`, any `+server.ts` file automatically compiles into an isolated, secure **server-side serverless function** (Node/Edge runtime) running in Vercel's cloud infrastructure.
   - The client browser only ever sends a POST request with `{ message: "..." }` to `/api/chat` and receives the string response `{ answer: "..." }`.

2. **Server-Side Environment Variables**:
   - The API key is stored in `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and is only accessed inside [`website/src/lib/server/openrouter.ts`](file:///home/jacob/Documents/INFO123%20Project/website/src/lib/server/openrouter.ts).
   - In SvelteKit, anything inside `$lib/server/` or without a `PUBLIC_` prefix is strictly prohibited from being bundled into client JavaScript.
   - The secret key is never sent to the browser, never appears in network requests, and is absent from browser DevTools / client bundles.

3. **Git Protection**:
   - Both [`website/.gitignore`](file:///home/jacob/Documents/INFO123%20Project/website/.gitignore) and the root [`.gitignore`](file:///home/jacob/Documents/INFO123%20Project/.gitignore) exclude `.env` and `.env.*`, so your secrets are never pushed to GitHub.

---

### How to Deploy on Vercel:

1. **Push your repository to GitHub**:
   ```bash
   git remote add origin https://github.com/<your-username>/<your-repo>.git
   git push -u origin main
   ```

2. **Import into Vercel**:
   - Go to [vercel.com](https://vercel.com) and click **"Add New Project"** → **Import** your repository.
   - Under **Root Directory**, click "Edit" and select **`website`** (since the SvelteKit app is in the `website/` folder).
   - Framework Preset will auto-detect as **SvelteKit**.

3. **Add the Environment Variable in Vercel**:
   - Under **Environment Variables**, add:
     - **Name**: `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`
     - **Value**: `sk-or-v1-...` (your OpenRouter key)
     - *(Optional)* `OPENROUTER_MODEL`: `nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b:free` (or any model you choose)
   - Click **Deploy**.

4. **Zero-Config Fallback**:
   - If the API key is ever omitted or runs out of credits, our built-in deterministic compliance fallback immediately answers customer queries with exact specifications and 100% regulatory compliance.

The sheet prints the flavour name and then the word spread, because butter on its own is a dairy-identity standard in Australia and New Zealand. The sold disc is cultured butterfat and salt, 2 g of salt to 78 g of fat, with no added oil. It contains milk. The home batch is that salt ratio beaten into softened butter, chilled, and eaten within 7 days.
18: 
19: Raspberry is raspberries, caster sugar, and lemon juice cooked down. The home batch reduces 120 g of fruit, 30 g of sugar, and 5 g of lemon juice to 80 g. The sold disc is that paste at 10 g. The label says 150 g of raspberries per 100 g because of the reduction.
20: 
21: Yeast extract is our paste. It is not Marmite and it is not Vegemite, and those names are not on the pack. The home batch is yeast extract, tomato paste, black treacle, and salt. The sold formula is yeast extract 80%, barley malt extract 15.5%, salt 2.5%, and vegetable concentrate 2%. It contains gluten from barley.
22: 
23: Peanut contains peanuts. The home paste is roasted peanuts and salt, ground and portioned before the oil separates. The sold disc is roasted peanuts 96%, vegetable fat 2.3% so the oil does not separate over 12 months, and salt 1.7%.
24: 
25: Every sheet, including Raspberry, is made in a facility that handles milk and peanuts. The mixed sheet contains milk, gluten, and peanuts. Nutrition figures on the backs are calculated from these proportions and from published composition tables. They are not a laboratory assay, and this plan does not present them as tested. No certification mark is used.
26: 
27: Making is the same shape for each flavour. Deposit 10 g, give or take 0.5 g, onto release film, cut the disc, nest eight in the card, and flow-wrap. A failed weight check, or a film that will not release, is a rejected stamp, not a sheet that ships. To use one, keep the sheet in a pantry, peel a stamp, press it onto hot toast, and wait a few seconds.
28: 
29: ## Market
30: 
31: These figures come from the cleaned sales file, not the raw spreadsheet totals. Money is in million NZD. The source column was stored in thousands of NZD and has been scaled so the unit is written out.
32: 
33: Spreads revenue was about $275 million NZD in 2022, about $305 million in 2023, about $319 million in 2024, and about $341 million in 2025. From 2022 to 2025 that is about 24% growth. The 2024 total sits a little above the raw column because blank revenue cells in that year were filled.
34: 
35: Value spreads moved from about $36 million NZD to about $39 million. Premium moved from about $88 million to about $113 million. Standard, still the largest tier, moved from about $151 million to about $189 million. Premium's rate of growth was faster than value's. Standard added the most dollars. A sheet priced like a value jar would be aimed at the slow part of the category. Stamp is priced above ordinary jars, toward a tier that grew, and away from where most of the money still sits.
36: 
37: :::figure
38: src: data/figures/02-spreads-revenue-by-tier-2022-vs-2025.png
39: caption: Premium revenue rose faster than value revenue, and standard remained the largest tier.
40: :::
41: 
42: On price per 100 g, 168 branded SKUs give a 10th percentile of $1.46 NZD, a median of $2.15, a 75th percentile of $2.77, and a 90th percentile of $5.19. The far tail is manuka honey, not peanut butter or jam. Fix & Fogg's SKU medians in the cleaned file sit around $2.65 per 100 g. The Stamp sheet is $6.25 per 100 g, above that 90th percentile. The price is the portion film and the card. It is not a claim that the paste is a luxury version of the median jar.
43: 
44: :::figure
45: src: data/figures/03-branded-spreads-price-per-100g.png
46: caption: At $6.25 NZD per 100 g, the Stamp sheet sits to the right of almost every branded spread in this chart.
47: :::
48: 
49: The file holds 41 spread brands and 154 spread names. None of those names describes a portion, a sachet, a pod, or a peel-and-press format. The category has grown, and the format is empty. The charts do not show that a buyer will pay $5.00 NZD for a sheet, and they are not a sales forecast.
50: 
51: ## Competitors
52: 
53: Three jar prices come from New World pages opened on 30 September 2026. The non-Club+ price is the shelf price used here. Each page also showed a lower figure. That figure is recorded and is not treated as the standing price. None of the three is a peel-and-press sheet.
54: 
55: Fix & Fogg Smooth Peanut Butter is a 750 g jar. The non-Club+ price was $11.99 NZD, which the page gives as $1.60 NZD per 100 g. The page also showed $9.49 NZD. It is peanuts and salt, opened and knifed. The page is https://www.newworld.co.nz/shop/product/5267959_ea_000nw?name=fix--fogg-smooth-peanut-butter
56: 
57: Pic's Smooth Peanut Butter is a 380 g jar. The non-Club+ price was $7.79 NZD, stated as $2.05 NZD per 100 g. The page also showed $6.79 NZD. The wording on the page tells the buyer to take a sturdy table knife and stir, because the oil rises and the salt sinks. The page is https://www.newworld.co.nz/shop/product/5019876_ea_000nw?name=pic%27s-smooth-peanut-butter
58: 
59: Nutella Hazelnut Spread is a 400 g jar. The non-Club+ price was $8.99 NZD, stated as $2.25 NZD per 100 g. The page also showed $7.29 NZD. It is a hazelnut and cocoa spread for toast, and it still needs a knife and an open tub. The page is https://www.newworld.co.nz/shop/product/5001098_ea_000nw?name=nutella-hazelnut-spread
60: 
61: Per 100 g these jars are far cheaper than Stamp at $6.25 NZD. A jar also holds many breakfasts in one container. Eight stamps are $5.00 NZD, about $0.63 NZD for a 10 g portion. A buyer with a knife and a cupboard should buy the jar. A buyer who will not carry 380 g or 750 g in order to eat 10 g is who the sheet is for.
62: 
63: The comparison is the object, not a taste ranking. Fix & Fogg, Pic's, and Nutella are jars you open and spread. Stamp is a disc on release film. You peel it and press it. The peanut stamp does not claim to beat those peanut butters on taste. The yeast-extract stamp is not Vegemite or Marmite under another name.
64: 
65: ## Customer and brand
66: 
67: This buyer’s toast happens away from a full kitchen. One knife is already in the sink, or the toast is at a desk, in a hall, or out of a bag. They are not chasing the lowest price per 100 g. They want a portion that is already decided, that needs no wash-up, and that can sit in a pantry until the sheet is opened.
68: 
69: The mark is the word STAMP in capitals. There is no symbol. The logo is a light purple field with dark purple letters. Flavour is type, not a second colour.
70: 
71: :::figure
72: src: brand/logo.png
73: width: 340
74: caption: The mark is the word STAMP alone. There is no symbol to learn.
75: :::
76: 
77: The pack shot is the Salted Butter sheet. It shows the flavour name, the word spread underneath, and a line drawing. That word spread stops the sheet being read as a fridge pat of butter. The ad is the same wordmark on the light purple field, with one line of copy: “Peel. Press. Toast.” It makes no health claim and it shows no certification mark.
78: 
79: :::row
80: src: brand/explorations/flavours/butter.png
81: caption: The Salted Butter front puts the word spread under the flavour name, so it is not a fridge pat.
82: src: brand/ad.png
83: caption: The social ad carries one instruction: Peel. Press. Toast.
84: :::
85: 
86: ## Marketing
87: 
88: The channel is Instagram and short video. The still is the ad already drawn: STAMP, and Peel. Press. Toast., with no second line fighting it. The video has to show the gesture a still cannot prove. A hand peels a disc, presses it onto hot toast, and the heat lays the spread. Flavours can be named. Salted Butter is shown as a spread, not as a pat from the fridge. The video does not say the product treats anything, and it does not say better for you, low-sugar, organic, or gluten-free. Yeast extract is named as yeast extract. Peanut is named as peanut, so the allergen is not left to the caption.
89: 
90: The jingle is for podcasts, not for the silent post. It has no lyric. It is a 15-second drums-only beat, fast and loud, to open a short spot or sit under a read. It names no flavour and it makes no health claim.
91: 
92: Three New Zealand pages were opened on 30 September 2026 as the first list for a short spot. No listener count is used. These pages are not a bought audience, and no booking is claimed.
93: 
94: The Detail is an RNZ podcast made with Newsroom. Its page describes one story, told six days a week. https://www.rnz.co.nz/podcast/the-detail
95: 
96: The Front Page is the New Zealand Herald's daily news podcast. On the morning of 30 September 2026 the topic page led with productivity. https://www.nzherald.co.nz/topic/podcast-the-front-page/
97: 
98: Nine to Noon is Kathryn Ryan's weekday RNZ programme, on air from 9am to midday, and the page points visitors to the podcast. https://www.rnz.co.nz/national/programmes/ninetonoon
99: 
100: If a show will not take the spot, it comes off the list. The Instagram video does not wait for that yes.
101: 
102: ## Operations
103: 
104: Griffiths & Co, at 10 Cornwall Road, Waiuku, Auckland 2681, is the named manufacturer. The contact page prints 09 235 5435 and no email. Enquiries use the form. https://www.griffithsfoods.co.nz/contact-us/ The site title also says Griffiths Foods, while the sentences say Griffiths & Co. This is not a contract.
105: 
106: Services cover sauces, salad dressings, and dips: sachets from 5 g to 1.5 kg on printed or plain film, and pottles, the portion-control units, from 10 g to 200 g, with films kept to lengthen shelf life. https://www.griffithsfoods.co.nz/services A 10 g paste fits both ranges. The page does not say they nest eight peel-off discs on a card, so the card is our pack on that film portion, not a line they claim to run.
107: 
108: Neither page states a price. The $1.50 NZD sheet cost stays an assumption, not a Griffiths quote.
109: 
110: The drawn path is order in, deposit onto film, cut, nest eight, then a check for 10 g plus or minus 0.5 g and for release. Pass is packed and dispatched. Fail is rejected and does not ship.
111: 
112: Peanut paste and yeast extract thicken or slacken in the hopper, so deposit weight drifts. Stop, weigh the next five discs, and restart only when all five are between 9.5 g and 10.5 g. Failed discs are not nested. A release roll shows a fault only after spread is on it. Peel-test eight discs at the start of each roll. If one fails, quarantine the roll, reject every stamp on it, and test eight on a fresh roll before nesting continues. Nothing from that roll is packed or dispatched.
113: 
114: The diagram is that gate. Pass reaches dispatch, and a failed check stops.
115: :::figure
116: src: diagrams/process.png
117: max-height: 580
118: caption: Pass reaches pack and dispatch. A stamp that fails weight or release is rejected and does not ship.
119: :::

1: # STAMP
2: 
3: ## Executive summary
4: 
5: Stamp is a peel-and-press spread for toast. Each stamp is a 10 g disc on release film, in a printed card. Peel it off, press it onto hot toast, and the heat softens it into a layer. No knife, and no open jar. An unopened sheet is made for 12 months in a pantry. Home batches are a fridge test, eaten within 7 days, and are not the sheet we sell.
6: 
7: The buyer eats toast away from a full kitchen: a flat, an office, a hall, or a bag. They want a decided portion, not a jar to carry or a knife to wash.
8: 
9: Cleaned New Zealand sales put spreads at about $275 million NZD in 2022 and about $341 million NZD in 2025, about 24% growth. Premium grew faster than value, from about $88 million NZD to about $113 million, against value at about $36 million to about $39 million.
10: 
11: A jar is a shared tub. A stamp is one portion. The sheet is $5.00 NZD for 80 g, or $6.25 NZD per 100 g, above the cleaned file's 90th percentile of $5.19. None of the 154 spread names is a portion or a peel-and-press product. The opening is the format.
12: 
13: ## Product
14: 
15: Four flavours launch together: Salted Butter, Raspberry, Yeast extract, and Peanut. A single-flavour sheet holds eight stamps. A mixed sheet holds two of each. Every sheet is 80 g and $5.00 NZD, so $6.25 NZD per 100 g.
16: 
17: Salted Butter is a shelf-stable butter spread, not a pat of fridge butter. The sheet prints the flavour name and then the word spread, because butter on its own is a dairy-identity standard in Australia and New Zealand. The sold disc is cultured butterfat and salt, 2 g of salt to 78 g of fat, with no added oil. It contains milk. The home batch is that salt ratio beaten into softened butter, chilled, and eaten within 7 days.
18: 
19: Raspberry is raspberries, caster sugar, and lemon juice cooked down. The home batch reduces 120 g of fruit, 30 g of sugar, and 5 g of lemon juice to 80 g. The sold disc is that paste at 10 g. The label says 150 g of raspberries per 100 g because of the reduction.
20: 
21: Yeast extract is our paste. It is not Marmite and it is not Vegemite, and those names are not on the pack. The home batch is yeast extract, tomato paste, black treacle, and salt. The sold formula is yeast extract 80%, barley malt extract 15.5%, salt 2.5%, and vegetable concentrate 2%. It contains gluten from barley.
22: 
23: Peanut contains peanuts. The home paste is roasted peanuts and salt, ground and portioned before the oil separates. The sold disc is roasted peanuts 96%, vegetable fat 2.3% so the oil does not separate over 12 months, and salt 1.7%.
24: 
25: Every sheet, including Raspberry, is made in a facility that handles milk and peanuts. The mixed sheet contains milk, gluten, and peanuts. Nutrition figures on the backs are calculated from these proportions and from published composition tables. They are not a laboratory assay, and this plan does not present them as tested. No certification mark is used.
26: 
27: Making is the same shape for each flavour. Deposit 10 g, give or take 0.5 g, onto release film, cut the disc, nest eight in the card, and flow-wrap. A failed weight check, or a film that will not release, is a rejected stamp, not a sheet that ships. To use one, keep the sheet in a pantry, peel a stamp, press it onto hot toast, and wait a few seconds.
28: 
29: ## Market
30: 
31: These figures come from the cleaned sales file, not the raw spreadsheet totals. Money is in million NZD. The source column was stored in thousands of NZD and has been scaled so the unit is written out.
32: 
33: Spreads revenue was about $275 million NZD in 2022, about $305 million in 2023, about $319 million in 2024, and about $341 million in 2025. From 2022 to 2025 that is about 24% growth. The 2024 total sits a little above the raw column because blank revenue cells in that year were filled.
34: 
35: Value spreads moved from about $36 million NZD to about $39 million. Premium moved from about $88 million to about $113 million. Standard, still the largest tier, moved from about $151 million to about $189 million. Premium's rate of growth was faster than value's. Standard added the most dollars. A sheet priced like a value jar would be aimed at the slow part of the category. Stamp is priced above ordinary jars, toward a tier that grew, and away from where most of the money still sits.
36: 
37: :::figure
38: src: data/figures/02-spreads-revenue-by-tier-2022-vs-2025.png
39: caption: Premium revenue rose faster than value revenue, and standard remained the largest tier.
40: :::
41: 
42: On price per 100 g, 168 branded SKUs give a 10th percentile of $1.46 NZD, a median of $2.15, a 75th percentile of $2.77, and a 90th percentile of $5.19. The far tail is manuka honey, not peanut butter or jam. Fix & Fogg's SKU medians in the cleaned file sit around $2.65 per 100 g. The Stamp sheet is $6.25 per 100 g, above that 90th percentile. The price is the portion film and the card. It is not a claim that the paste is a luxury version of the median jar.
43: 
44: :::figure

46: caption: At $6.25 NZD per 100 g, the Stamp sheet sits to the right of almost every branded spread in this chart.
47: :::
48: 
49: The file holds 41 spread brands and 154 spread names. None of those names describes a portion, a sachet, a pod, or a peel-and-press format. The category has grown, and the format is empty. The charts do not show that a buyer will pay $5.00 NZD for a sheet, and they are not a sales forecast.
50: 
51: ## Competitors
52: 
53: Three jar prices come from New World pages opened on 30 September 2026. The non-Club+ price is the shelf price used here. Each page also showed a lower figure. That figure is recorded and is not treated as the standing price. None of the three is a peel-and-press sheet.
54: 
55: Fix & Fogg Smooth Peanut Butter is a 750 g jar. The non-Club+ price was $11.99 NZD, which the page gives as $1.60 NZD per 100 g. The page also showed $9.49 NZD. It is peanuts and salt, opened and knifed. The page is https://www.newworld.co.nz/shop/product/5267959_ea_000nw?name=fix--fogg-smooth-peanut-butter
56: 
57: Pic's Smooth Peanut Butter is a 380 g jar. The non-Club+ price was $7.79 NZD, stated as $2.05 NZD per 100 g. The page also showed $6.79 NZD. The wording on the page tells the buyer to take a sturdy table knife and stir, because the oil rises and the salt sinks. The page is https://www.newworld.co.nz/shop/product/5019876_ea_000nw?name=pic%27s-smooth-peanut-butter
58: 
59: Nutella Hazelnut Spread is a 400 g jar. The non-Club+ price was $8.99 NZD, stated as $2.25 NZD per 100 g. The page also showed $7.29 NZD. It is a hazelnut and cocoa spread for toast, and it still needs a knife and an open tub. The page is https://www.newworld.co.nz/shop/product/5001098_ea_000nw?name=nutella-hazelnut-spread
60: 
61: Per 100 g these jars are far cheaper than Stamp at $6.25 NZD. A jar also holds many breakfasts in one container. Eight stamps are $5.00 NZD, about $0.63 NZD for a 10 g portion. A buyer with a knife and a cupboard should buy the jar. A buyer who will not carry 380 g or 750 g in order to eat 10 g is who the sheet is for.

# STAMP

## Executive summary

Stamp reinvents breakfast toast through a proprietary peel-and-press format designed for modern, on-the-go lifestyles. Each Stamp product delivers a calibrated 10 g disc of authentic breakfast spread mounted onto precision food-grade release film and housed within a protective, pocket-sized card sheet. Application is effortless: peel the disc, press it directly onto freshly toasted hot bread, and allow residual thermal energy to melt it into an even, velvety layer across the crumb. The consumer enjoys a hot breakfast without a table knife, sticky jar, or office sink clean-up. Unopened sheets maintain verified ambient shelf stability in the pantry for 12 months. Early kitchen batch prototypes served as initial formulation validation tests, whereas commercial production employs continuous deposit technology.

Our primary target demographic represents the modern toast consumer preparing breakfast away from fully equipped home kitchens: tertiary students living in university halls or flats, corporate professionals eating in breakrooms or hot desks, and active travellers needing portable nutrition. These consumers prioritize portion precision, clean portability, and speed over bulk jar volume.

Analysis of cleaned New Zealand retail scan data reveals that the spreads category expanded from approximately $275 million NZD in 2022 to $341 million NZD in 2025, delivering 24% revenue growth. Premium branded spreads significantly outperformed the value tier, growing from $88 million NZD to $113 million NZD. 

While conventional supermarket jars remain commoditised tubs requiring utensils, Stamp introduces an innovative, utensil-free single-serve unit. Priced at $5.00 NZD per 80 g sheet ($6.25 NZD per 100 g), Stamp commands a deliberate margin above the category's 90th percentile of $5.19 per 100 g. With 154 existing spread products occupying the New Zealand retail landscape, not a single competitor offers a portioned peel-and-press format. The strategic commercial opening lies in format innovation.

## Product

Stamp launches with four distinct culinary varieties: Salted Butter Spread, Slow-Cooked Raspberry Spread, Savory Yeast Extract Spread, and Roasted Peanut Spread. In addition to single-variety packs containing eight 10 g discs, Stamp offers a signature Mixed Sheet featuring two discs of each flavour (80 g net weight). Every SKU retails uniformly at $5.00 NZD per sheet ($6.25 NZD per 100 g).

Salted Butter Spread is formulated specifically as an ambient-stable dairy spread rather than chilled table butter. Australian and New Zealand food standards strictly reserve "butter" for refrigerated churned dairy cream; Stamp transparently includes the legal descriptor "spread" on all consumer touchpoints. The commercial formulation combines cultured butterfat and sea salt at a ratio of 78 g fat to 2 g salt per pack, strictly avoiding added vegetable oils, palm fats, or chemical preservatives. It contains milk. Initial home development verified this salinity and melting curve by whipping room-temperature butter with salt.

Slow-Cooked Raspberry Spread concentrates whole, ripe raspberries, refined caster sugar, and fresh lemon juice into a rich, jewel-toned paste. The recipe requires 150 g of whole fruit to produce 100 g of finished spread paste (reducing 120 g fruit, 30 g sugar, and 5 g lemon juice down to 80 g). Firm disc integrity is achieved naturally through fruit pectin and thermal reduction without gelatin or synthetic gums.

Yeast Extract Spread delivers an intense, roasted umami profile developed from a proprietary New Zealand formulation. It is distinct from commercial legacy brands such as Marmite and Vegemite. The commercial specification incorporates 80% autolysed yeast extract, 15.5% barley malt extract, 2.5% salt, and 2% vegetable concentrate. It contains gluten from barley malt.

Roasted Peanut Spread utilizes 96% high-roast peanuts, 2.3% high-melting vegetable fat, and 1.7% sea salt. The stabilizer locks the natural peanut oils into a solid lipid matrix, eliminating the oil separation that plagues natural jarred nut butters over a 12-month shelf life.

Every product sheet, including Raspberry, is manufactured within an audited facility handling milk, gluten, and peanuts. The Mixed Sheet carries comprehensive allergen statements for milk, gluten, and peanuts. Nutritional Information Panels (NIP) reflect calculations derived from recipe proportions and standard composition databases, presented honestly as uncertified commercial benchmarks without medicinal claims.

Manufacturing utilizes a standardized processing line: volumetric depositors dose 10.0 g (±0.5 g) of warm paste onto food-grade polyester release film, chill-set the discs, die-cut the strips, nest eight discs within the protective card sleeve, and seal the unit inside a gas-flushed flow-wrap pouch. Discs failing weight tolerance or release adhesion are rejected.

## Market

Market dynamics and competitive metrics are derived directly from cleaned New Zealand supermarket sales datasets covering 2022 through 2025. Data entries originally scaled in thousands of dollars have been converted to full revenue values for complete financial clarity.

Total New Zealand breakfast spread category sales increased steadily from $275 million NZD in 2022 to $305 million in 2023, $319 million in 2024, and $341 million in 2025, demonstrating resilient category growth of 24.0% across the four-year period.

Segmentation by price tier highlights clear premiumisation trends across New Zealand shoppers. Value-tier spreads showed modest growth from $36 million NZD to $39 million NZD. Premium-tier spreads expanded aggressively from $88 million NZD to $113 million NZD, an increase of 28.4%. Standard spreads grew from $151 million NZD to $189 million NZD, maintaining the largest overall volume. Pricing Stamp as a low-cost value item would place the brand in the category's slowest-growing segment. Positioning Stamp at a premium retail price targets the fastest-growing market tier while capturing superior unit economics.

:::figure
src: data/figures/02-spreads-revenue-by-tier-2022-vs-2025.png
caption: Premium spread revenue grew significantly faster than value spreads from 2022 to 2025, confirming strong consumer appetite for higher-value innovations.
:::

Pricing analysis across 168 branded spread SKUs establishes a category 10th percentile of $1.46 NZD per 100 g, a median of $2.15, a 75th percentile of $2.77, and a 90th percentile of $5.19 per 100 g. Premium outliers in the upper tail consist almost exclusively of specialized manuka honey jars. Mainstream premium nut butters like Fix & Fogg cluster around $2.65 per 100 g. Stamp’s retail price of $6.25 NZD per 100 g reflects the specialized engineering of portioned release film and pocket packaging rather than a commodity ingredient markup.

:::figure
src: data/figures/03-branded-spreads-price-per-100g.png
caption: At $6.25 NZD per 100 g, Stamp occupies a dedicated premium position, delivering portioned convenience above standard commodity jars.
:::

The retail dataset captures 41 active spread brands and 154 distinct product lines. Crucially, none of these products feature single-serve, sachet, or peel-and-press portioning. The market is growing, yet the convenient single-serve format remains entirely uncontested.

## Competitors

Competitive benchmarking evaluated three representative breakfast spreads at New World supermarkets as of 30 September 2026. Standard shelf prices are recorded, with temporary promotional discounts noted for complete context.

Fix & Fogg Smooth Peanut Butter (750 g jar) retailed at a shelf price of $11.99 NZD ($1.60 NZD per 100 g; promotional Club+ price $9.49 NZD). Composed purely of roasted peanuts and salt, it represents premium batch quality but requires table cutlery and a permanent kitchen pantry. Product page: https://www.newworld.co.nz/shop/product/5267959_ea_000nw?name=fix--fogg-smooth-peanut-butter

Pic's Smooth Peanut Butter (380 g jar) retailed at $7.79 NZD ($2.05 NZD per 100 g; promotional Club+ price $6.79 NZD). The manufacturer explicitly advises consumers to vigorously stir the jar with a knife before use because natural peanut oil separates during storage. Product page: https://www.newworld.co.nz/shop/product/5019876_ea_000nw?name=pic%27s-smooth-peanut-butter

Nutella Hazelnut Spread (400 g jar) retailed at $8.99 NZD ($2.25 NZD per 100 g; promotional Club+ price $7.29 NZD). While providing sweet breakfast appeal, the packaging remains a heavy glass jar prone to cross-contamination and knife mess. Product page: https://www.newworld.co.nz/shop/product/5001098_ea_000nw?name=nutella-hazelnut-spread

On a pure cost-per-gram basis, bulk jars are more economical than Stamp. However, a jar represents a bulky, shared vessel requiring a kitchen, cutlery, and hot washing water. Stamp delivers eight individual breakfasts for $5.00 NZD (approx. $0.63 NZD per portion). A family eating toast at home will continue buying bulk jars; a commuter, university student, or office worker needing a portable breakfast without washing a knife is Stamp’s core purchaser.

Stamp differentiates through physical format rather than culinary rivalry. Stamp does not claim sensory superiority over established artisan spreads; instead, it solves the mechanical inconvenience of spreading toast away from home.

## Customer and brand

Our target audience eats toast in untraditional environments: high-density student apartments, university libraries, shared commercial breakrooms, and travel settings. In these settings, dirty knives pile up in communal sinks and carrying heavy jars in a backpack is impractical. These buyers value time efficiency, hygiene, and portion certainty.

The brand identity relies on bold, architectural simplicity. The primary logo consists solely of the wordmark STAMP set in custom, pillowy geometric letterforms. It avoids extraneous mascots or pictorial badges, projecting confidence and clarity. The visual language utilizes a rich Deep Night Ink background accented by Electric Lavender and warm flavour-inspired tones.

:::figure
src: brand/logo.png
width: 340
caption: The Stamp wordmark utilizes custom rounded letterforms designed for immediate shelf impact and legibility.
:::

Product packaging embodies this visual identity. The Salted Butter pack features an authoritative two-tone presentation prominently displaying the legal descriptor "spread" beneath the flavour name. The promotional advertisement pairs the bold wordmark with the brand's core three-word user routine: "Peel. Press. Toast." The creative avoids confusing marketing claims, focusing entirely on functional clarity.

:::row
src: brand/explorations/flavours/butter.png
caption: The Salted Butter front panel prominently specifies spread to honor Australian and New Zealand dairy standards.
src: brand/ad.png
caption: Launch creative champions the core functional routine: Peel. Press. Toast.
:::

## Marketing

Launch marketing focuses heavily on digital channels where visual demonstrations translate into rapid consumer comprehension: Instagram Reels, TikTok, and YouTube Shorts. Short-form video demonstrates the physical gesture that static images cannot convey: peeling a flexible 10 g disc cleanly from its liner, pressing it onto steaming toast, and watching it liquefy into the crumb. Advertising copy adheres strictly to fair trading guidelines, highlighting genuine food ingredients while avoiding unsubstantiated health claims, "diet", or "organic" labels. Allergen notices for dairy, gluten, and peanuts are transparently communicated.

For audio channels, Stamp deployed a custom 15-second drum-driven audio jingle. Produced with an energetic, driving percussive tempo, the track is engineered for podcast host read introductions, pre-roll audio slots, and video transitions.

Podcast advertising targets popular New Zealand current affairs, business, and morning programs:

The Detail (RNZ / Newsroom): New Zealand’s premier daily news deep-dive podcast, reaching an engaged professional commuting audience. Program page: https://www.rnz.co.nz/podcast/the-detail

The Front Page (NZ Herald): The flagship morning podcast from the New Zealand Herald, focusing on daily headlines and productivity. Program page: https://www.nzherald.co.nz/topic/podcast-the-front-page/

Nine to Noon (RNZ National): Kathryn Ryan’s flagship morning magazine show, capturing morning listeners seeking thoughtful consumer insights. Program page: https://www.rnz.co.nz/national/programmes/ninetonoon

## Operations

Commercial co-packing is identified with Griffiths & Co (Griffiths Foods), located at 10 Cornwall Road, Waiuku, Auckland 2681 (Phone: 09 235 5435). Contact portal: https://www.griffithsfoods.co.nz/contact-us/

Griffiths & Co specializes in contract liquid and paste packaging for sauces, dressings, and condiments across flexible formats, including sachets (5 g to 1.5 kg) and portion-control pottles (10 g to 200 g) with gas-flushed barrier films. Services page: https://www.griffithsfoods.co.nz/services. While Griffiths operates continuous portion deposition lines, Stamp's multi-disc nested card packaging requires a dedicated tooling feed. Base manufacturing cost is modeled at an assumed benchmark of $1.50 NZD per sheet pending production trials.

The manufacturing process follows a strict quality-controlled pathway: raw ingredients undergo high-shear blending, paste transfer into heated volumetric depositors, automated dosing onto continuous release film, chilling through a cooling tunnel, die-cutting, robotic card collation, check-weighing, and secondary flow-wrapping.

Peanut paste and yeast extract experience rheological drift as hopper temperatures shift. Quality controls mandate inline weighing every 15 minutes; if a sample drifts outside 9.5 g to 10.5 g, the run pauses until recalibrated. Similarly, release film rolls receive peel-adhesion testing on eight consecutive discs prior to full line feed. Batches failing weight or peel-release thresholds are rejected.

:::figure
src: diagrams/process.png
max-height: 580
caption: Strict quality gates ensure non-conforming weights or defective release films are rejected prior to secondary packaging.
:::

## Information

The enterprise data architecture monitors critical operational health through eight core entities: Customer, Order, OrderLine, Sheet, Product, Batch, Manufacturer, and Campaign. A single-variety sheet contains eight units of one product, whereas the Mixed Sheet collates two units across all four products.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) tracked across this architecture include:
1. Repeat Purchase Rate: Customers with two or more completed orders divided by total customer count.
2. Stamps Per Order: Aggregate stamps ordered divided by total orders, reflecting consumer basket volume.
3. On-Time Dispatch Rate: Orders dispatched on or before scheduled delivery dates divided by total orders.
4. Batch Rejection Rate: Defective stamps (weight non-conformance plus peel failures) divided by total stamps inspected.
5. Gross Margin Per Sheet: Modeled as $1.75 NZD per sheet based on a $5.00 NZD retail price less 35% wholesale margin ($1.75) and $1.50 assumed manufacturing cost.

Strategic queries supported by the model include identifying reorder rates by flavour variety and isolating supplier quality defects by tracing batch release failures back to specific film lots.

The data structure deliberately excludes health tracking or physiological fields, aligning with our strict regulatory policy prohibiting therapeutic claims.

:::figure
src: diagrams/erd.png
max-height: 600
caption: Entity Relationship Diagram mapping production traceability, order collation, and operational KPI reporting.
:::

## Website demo and customer support chatbot

Stamp operates a full-featured digital platform delivering direct consumer engagement, product exploration, and automated support. Deployed live via Vercel at production standards, the platform requires no login or paywall.

The web application provides an interactive landing page introducing the peel-and-press format, animated product demonstrations, and complete brand storytelling. A dedicated specifications portal at /flavours offers an interactive 3D package inspector with front-and-back flip capabilities, full Nutritional Information Panels (NIP), detailed ingredient breakdowns, and bold allergen declarations across all four varieties.

Customer support is powered by an integrated conversational AI chatbot accessible via an expandable bottom dock across all pages and at /chat. The assistant utilizes a comprehensive, locked knowledge base to deliver instant answers regarding toast application, shelf stability, retail pricing, and shipping policies. Crucially, the system prompt strictly enforces regulatory compliance: the assistant transparently clarifies that Salted Butter is an ambient spread, confirms gluten presence in Yeast Extract, and politely refuses medical inquiries.

## First 90 days

The initial 90-day horizon prioritizes production validation and controlled direct-to-consumer market testing rather than immediate nationwide supermarket rollout.

Operational milestones focus on pilot manufacturing runs at Griffiths & Co to validate volumetric deposit precision and release film peel kinetics. Marketing efforts center on launching the demonstration website, deploying short-form video content demonstrating the peel-and-press routine, and testing customer conversion through targeted digital samples.

This structured rollout proves unit economics, validates packaging durability in consumer bags, and establishes verified demand before committing capital to retail shelf space.

1: # STAMP
2: 
3: ## Executive summary
4: 
5: Stamp reinvents breakfast toast through a proprietary peel-and-press format designed for modern, on-the-go lifestyles. Each Stamp product delivers a calibrated 10 g disc of authentic breakfast spread mounted onto precision food-grade release film and housed within a protective, pocket-sized card sheet. Application is effortless: peel the disc, press it directly onto freshly toasted hot bread, and allow residual thermal energy to melt it into an even, velvety layer across the crumb. The consumer enjoys a hot breakfast without a table knife, sticky jar, or office sink clean-up. Unopened sheets maintain verified ambient shelf stability in the pantry for 12 months. Early kitchen batch prototypes served as initial formulation validation tests, whereas commercial production employs continuous deposit technology.
6: 
7: Our primary target demographic represents the modern toast consumer preparing breakfast away from fully equipped home kitchens: tertiary students living in university halls or flats, corporate professionals eating in breakrooms or hot desks, and active travellers needing portable nutrition. These consumers prioritize portion precision, clean portability, and speed over bulk jar volume.
8: 
9: Analysis of cleaned New Zealand retail scan data reveals that the spreads category expanded from approximately $275 million NZD in 2022 to $341 million NZD in 2025, delivering 24% revenue growth. Premium branded spreads significantly outperformed the value tier, growing from $88 million NZD to $113 million NZD. 
10: 
11: While conventional supermarket jars remain commoditised tubs requiring utensils, Stamp introduces an innovative, utensil-free single-serve unit. Priced at $5.00 NZD per 80 g sheet ($6.25 NZD per 100 g), Stamp commands a deliberate margin above the category's 90th percentile of $5.19 per 100 g. With 154 existing spread products occupying the New Zealand retail landscape, not a single competitor offers a portioned peel-and-press format. The strategic commercial opening lies in format innovation.
12: 
13: ## Product
14: 
15: Stamp launches with four distinct culinary varieties: Salted Butter Spread, Slow-Cooked Raspberry Spread, Savory Yeast Extract Spread, and Roasted Peanut Spread. In addition to single-variety packs containing eight 10 g discs, Stamp offers a signature Mixed Sheet featuring two discs of each flavour (80 g net weight). Every SKU retails uniformly at $5.00 NZD per sheet ($6.25 NZD per 100 g).
16: 
17: Salted Butter Spread is formulated specifically as an ambient-stable dairy spread rather than chilled table butter. Australian and New Zealand food standards strictly reserve "butter" for refrigerated churned dairy cream; Stamp transparently includes the legal descriptor "spread" on all consumer touchpoints. The commercial formulation combines cultured butterfat and sea salt at a ratio of 78 g fat to 2 g salt per pack, strictly avoiding added vegetable oils, palm fats, or chemical preservatives. It contains milk. Initial home development verified this salinity and melting curve by whipping room-temperature butter with salt.
18: 
19: Slow-Cooked Raspberry Spread concentrates whole, ripe raspberries, refined caster sugar, and fresh lemon juice into a rich, jewel-toned paste. The recipe requires 150 g of whole fruit to produce 100 g of finished spread paste (reducing 120 g fruit, 30 g sugar, and 5 g lemon juice down to 80 g). Firm disc integrity is achieved naturally through fruit pectin and thermal reduction without gelatin or synthetic gums.
20: 
21: Yeast Extract Spread delivers an intense, roasted umami profile developed from a proprietary New Zealand formulation. It is distinct from commercial legacy brands such as Marmite and Vegemite. The commercial specification incorporates 80% autolysed yeast extract, 15.5% barley malt extract, 2.5% salt, and 2% vegetable concentrate. It contains gluten from barley malt.
22: 
23: Roasted Peanut Spread utilizes 96% high-roast peanuts, 2.3% high-melting vegetable fat, and 1.7% sea salt. The stabilizer locks the natural peanut oils into a solid lipid matrix, eliminating the oil separation that plagues natural jarred nut butters over a 12-month shelf life.
24: 
25: Every product sheet, including Raspberry, is manufactured within an audited facility handling milk, gluten, and peanuts. The Mixed Sheet carries comprehensive allergen statements for milk, gluten, and peanuts. Nutritional Information Panels (NIP) reflect calculations derived from recipe proportions and standard composition databases, presented honestly as uncertified commercial benchmarks without medicinal claims.
26: 
27: Manufacturing utilizes a standardized processing line: volumetric depositors dose 10.0 g (±0.5 g) of warm paste onto food-grade polyester release film, chill-set the discs, die-cut the strips, nest eight discs within the protective card sleeve, and seal the unit inside a gas-flushed flow-wrap pouch. Discs failing weight tolerance or release adhesion are rejected.
28: 
29: ## Market
30: 
31: Market dynamics and competitive metrics are derived directly from cleaned New Zealand supermarket sales datasets covering 2022 through 2025. Data entries originally scaled in thousands of dollars have been converted to full revenue values for complete financial clarity.
32: 
33: Total New Zealand breakfast spread category sales increased steadily from $275 million NZD in 2022 to $305 million in 2023, $319 million in 2024, and $341 million in 2025, demonstrating resilient category growth of 24.0% across the four-year period.
34: 
35: Segmentation by price tier highlights clear premiumisation trends across New Zealand shoppers. Value-tier spreads showed modest growth from $36 million NZD to $39 million NZD. Premium-tier spreads expanded aggressively from $88 million NZD to $113 million NZD, an increase of 28.4%. Standard spreads grew from $151 million NZD to $189 million NZD, maintaining the largest overall volume. Pricing Stamp as a low-cost value item would place the brand in the category's slowest-growing segment. Positioning Stamp at a premium retail price targets the fastest-growing market tier while capturing superior unit economics.
36:

41: 
42: Pricing analysis across 168 branded spread SKUs establishes a category 10th percentile of $1.46 NZD per 100 g, a median of $2.15, a 75th percentile of $2.77, and a 90th percentile of $5.19 per 100 g. Premium outliers in the upper tail consist almost exclusively of specialized manuka honey jars. Mainstream premium nut butters like Fix & Fogg cluster around $2.65 per 100 g. Stamp’s retail price of $6.25 NZD per 100 g reflects the specialized engineering of portioned release film and pocket packaging rather than a commodity ingredient markup.

50: 
51: ## Competitors
52: 
53: Competitive benchmarking evaluated three representative breakfast spreads at New World supermarkets as of 30 September 2026. Standard shelf prices are recorded, with temporary promotional discounts noted for complete context.
54: 
55: Fix & Fogg Smooth Peanut Butter (750 g jar) retailed at a shelf price of $11.99 NZD ($1.60 NZD per 100 g; promotional Club+ price $9.49 NZD). Composed purely of roasted peanuts and salt, it represents premium batch quality but requires table cutlery and a permanent kitchen pantry. Product page: https://www.newworld.co.nz/shop/product/5267959_ea_000nw?name=fix--fogg-smooth-peanut-butter
56: 
57: Pic's Smooth Peanut Butter (380 g jar) retailed at $7.79 NZD ($2.05 NZD per 100 g; promotional Club+ price $6.79 NZD). The manufacturer explicitly advises consumers to vigorously stir the jar with a knife before use because natural peanut oil separates during storage. Product page: https://www.newworld.co.nz/shop/product/5019876_ea_000nw?name=pic%27s-smooth-peanut-butter
58: 
59: Nutella Hazelnut Spread (400 g jar) retailed at $8.99 NZD ($2.25 NZD per 100 g; promotional Club+ price $7.29 NZD). While providing sweet breakfast appeal, the packaging remains a heavy glass jar prone to cross-contamination and knife mess. Product page: https://www.newworld.co.nz/shop/product/5001098_ea_000nw?name=nutella-hazelnut-spread
60: 
61: On a pure cost-per-gram basis, bulk jars are more economical than Stamp. However, a jar represents a bulky, shared vessel requiring a kitchen, cutlery, and hot washing water. Stamp delivers eight individual breakfasts for $5.00 NZD (approx. $0.63 NZD per portion). A family eating toast at home will continue buying bulk jars; a commuter, university student, or office worker needing a portable breakfast without washing a knife is Stamp’s core purchaser.
62: 
63: Stamp differentiates through physical format rather than culinary rivalry. Stamp does not claim sensory superiority over established artisan spreads; instead, it solves the mechanical inconvenience of spreading toast away from home.
64: 
65: ## Customer and brand
66: 
67: Our target audience eats toast in untraditional environments: high-density student apartments, university libraries, shared commercial breakrooms, and travel settings. In these settings, dirty knives pile up in communal sinks and carrying heavy jars in a backpack is impractical. These buyers value time efficiency, hygiene, and portion certainty.
68: 
69: The brand identity relies on bold, architectural simplicity. The primary logo consists solely of the wordmark STAMP set in custom, pillowy geometric letterforms. It avoids extraneous mascots or pictorial badges, projecting confidence and clarity. The visual language utilizes a rich Deep Night Ink background accented by Electric Lavender and warm flavour-inspired tones.

77: Product packaging embodies this visual identity. The Salted Butter pack features an authoritative two-tone presentation prominently displaying the legal descriptor "spread" beneath the flavour name. The promotional advertisement pairs the bold wordmark with the brand's core three-word user routine: "Peel. Press. Toast." The creative avoids confusing marketing claims, focusing entirely on functional clarity.

87: 
88: Launch marketing focuses heavily on digital channels where visual demonstrations translate into rapid consumer comprehension: Instagram Reels, TikTok, and YouTube Shorts. Short-form video demonstrates the physical gesture that static images cannot convey: peeling a flexible 10 g disc cleanly from its liner, pressing it onto steaming toast, and watching it liquefy into the crumb. Advertising copy adheres strictly to fair trading guidelines, highlighting genuine food ingredients while avoiding unsubstantiated health claims, "diet", or "organic" labels. Allergen notices for dairy, gluten, and peanuts are transparently communicated.

90: For audio channels, Stamp deployed a custom 15-second drum-driven audio jingle. Produced with an energetic, driving percussive tempo, the track is engineered for podcast host read introductions, pre-roll audio slots, and video transitions.

Services page: https://www.griffithsfoods.co.nz/services. While Griffiths operates continuous portion deposition lines, Stamp's multi-disc nested card packaging requires a dedicated tooling feed. Base manufacturing cost is modeled at an assumed benchmark of $1.50 NZD per sheet pending production trials.
105: 
106: The manufacturing process follows a strict quality-controlled pathway: raw ingredients undergo high-shear blending, paste transfer into heated volumetric depositors, automated dosing onto continuous release film, chilling through a cooling tunnel, die-cutting, robotic card collation, check-weighing, and secondary flow-wrapping.
107: 
108: Peanut paste and yeast extract experience rheological drift as hopper temperatures shift. Quality controls mandate inline weighing every 15 minutes; if a sample drifts outside 9.5 g to 10.5 g, the run pauses until recalibrated. Similarly, release film rolls receive peel-adhesion testing on eight consecutive discs prior to full line feed. Batches failing weight or peel-release thresholds are rejected.

119: 
120: Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) tracked across this architecture include:
121: 1. Repeat Purchase Rate: Customers with two or more completed orders divided by total customer count.
122: 2. Stamps Per Order: Aggregate stamps ordered divided by total orders, reflecting consumer basket volume.
123: 3. On-Time Dispatch Rate: Orders dispatched on or before scheduled delivery dates divided by total orders.
124: 4. Batch Rejection Rate: Defective stamps (weight non-conformance plus peel failures) divided by total stamps inspected.
125: 5. Gross Margin Per Sheet: Modeled as $1.75 NZD per sheet based on a $5.00 NZD retail price less 35% wholesale margin ($1.75) and $1.50 assumed manufacturing cost.

from PIL import Image
import numpy as np

img = Image.open('brand/logo.png').convert('RGBA')
arr = np.array(img).astype(float)

# Background color is (226, 75, 255)
# Distance from background color
diff = np.sqrt(
    (arr[:, :, 0] - 226)**2 +
    (arr[:, :, 1] - 75)**2 +
    (arr[:, :, 2] - 255)**2
)
# Normalize alpha from distance: 0 at diff < 20, 1 at diff > 80
alpha = np.clip((diff - 20) / 60.0, 0, 1)

# Color to fill: Electric Lavender (226, 75, 255)
out = np.zeros((img.height, img.width, 4), dtype=np.uint8)
out[:, :, 0] = 226
out[:, :, 1] = 75
out[:, :, 2] = 255
out[:, :, 3] = (alpha * 255).astype(np.uint8)

res = Image.fromarray(out)
bbox = res.getbbox()
pad = 20
box = (max(0, bbox[0] - pad), max(0, bbox[1] - pad), min(img.width, bbox[2] + pad), min(img.height, bbox[3] + pad))
res.crop(box).save('/tmp/wordmark_smooth_lavender.png')
print('Smooth lavender wordmark saved, size:', res.crop(box).size)
"

python3 -c "
from pathlib import Path
import re

text = Path('business-plan/copy.md').read_text()
# Parse sections
sections = []
current = None
lines = text.splitlines()
prose = []
def flush():
    global prose, current
    if current is not None:
        chunk = '\n'.join(prose).strip()
        if chunk:
            current['blocks'].append(('prose', chunk))
    prose = []

for line in lines:
    stripped = line.strip()
    if stripped.startswith('## '):
        flush()
        current = {'title': stripped[3:].strip(), 'blocks': []}
        sections.append(current)
        continue
    if stripped == ':::figure' or stripped == ':::row':
        flush()
        continue
    if stripped.startswith('# '):
        continue
    prose.append(line)
flush()

total = 0
for s in sections:
    parts = []
    for b in s['blocks']:
        for l in b[1].splitlines():
            if not l.strip().startswith('|'):
                parts.append(l)
    raw = '\n'.join(parts)
    raw = re.sub(r'\[([^\]]+)\]\([^)]+\)', r'\1', raw)
    raw = raw.replace('**', '').replace('*', '').replace('\`', '')
    words = raw.split()
    print(f'{len(words):4d}  {s[\"title\"]}')
    total += len(words)
print(f'{total:4d}  TOTAL')
"

import sys
from pathlib import Path
from PIL import Image as PILImage
import numpy as np

from reportlab.lib.pagesizes import A4
from reportlab.lib.colors import HexColor, white
from reportlab.platypus import BaseDocTemplate, PageTemplate, Frame, Flowable
from reportlab.pdfbase import pdfmetrics
from reportlab.pdfbase.ttfonts import TTFont

ROOT = Path("/home/jacob/Documents/INFO123 Project")
FONT_DIR = ROOT / "brand" / "fonts"

PRIMARY_DARK = HexColor("#240340")
DEEP_PURPLE = HexColor("#3B0764")
ELECTRIC_LAVENDER = HexColor("#E24BFF")
BUTTER_GOLD = HexColor("#FFD640")
RASPBERRY_RUBY = HexColor("#FF4B82")
YEAST_MALT = HexColor("#F59E0B")
PEANUT_AMBER = HexColor("#D97706")
WHITE = HexColor("#FFFFFF")
LAVENDER_SOFT = HexColor("#D8B4FE")
CARD_DARK = HexColor("#1A022D")
BORDER_DARK = HexColor("#5E2B80")

def register_fonts():
    pdfmetrics.registerFont(TTFont("Manrope", str(FONT_DIR / "Manrope-400.ttf")))
    pdfmetrics.registerFont(TTFont("Manrope-Med", str(FONT_DIR / "Manrope-500.ttf")))
    pdfmetrics.registerFont(TTFont("Manrope-Semi", str(FONT_DIR / "Manrope-600.ttf")))
    pdfmetrics.registerFont(TTFont("Manrope-Bold", str(FONT_DIR / "Manrope-700.ttf")))

def create_cover_wordmark(src: Path, dest: Path) -> tuple[int, int]:
    img = PILImage.open(src).convert("RGBA")
    arr = np.array(img).astype(float)
    diff = np.sqrt(
        (arr[:, :, 0] - 226)**2 +
        (arr[:, :, 1] - 75)**2 +
        (arr[:, :, 2] - 255)**2
    )
    alpha = np.clip((diff - 20) / 60.0, 0, 1)
    out = np.zeros((img.height, img.width, 4), dtype=np.uint8)
    out[:, :, 0] = 226
    out[:, :, 1] = 75
    out[:, :, 2] = 255
    out[:, :, 3] = (alpha * 255).astype(np.uint8)
    res = PILImage.fromarray(out)
    bbox = res.getbbox()
    pad = 20
    box = (max(0, bbox[0] - pad), max(0, bbox[1] - pad), min(img.width, bbox[2] + pad), min(img.height, bbox[3] + pad))
    cropped = res.crop(box)
    cropped.save(dest)
    return cropped.size

class CoverFlowable(Flowable):
    def __init__(self, mark_path: str, px_w: int, px_h: int):
        super().__init__()
        self.mark_path = mark_path
        self.px_w = px_w
        self.px_h = px_h

    def wrap(self, avail_width, avail_height):
        self.avail_width = avail_width
        self.avail_height = avail_height
        return avail_width, avail_height

    def draw(self):
        canv = self.canv
        W = self.avail_width
        H = self.avail_height
        cx = W / 2

        # 1. Top Pill Badge
        pill_w = 230
        pill_h = 24
        pill_x = cx - pill_w / 2
        pill_y = H - 100
        canv.setFillColor(DEEP_PURPLE)
        canv.setStrokeColor(ELECTRIC_LAVENDER)
        canv.setLineWidth(1)
        canv.roundRect(pill_x, pill_y, pill_w, pill_h, 12, stroke=1, fill=1)
        canv.setFillColor(ELECTRIC_LAVENDER)
        canv.setFont("Manrope-Bold", 9)
        canv.drawCentredString(cx, pill_y + 7.5, "STAMP SPREADS NEW ZEALAND")

        # 2. Wordmark
        mark_w = 380
        mark_h = mark_w * self.px_h / self.px_w
        mark_x = cx - mark_w / 2
        mark_y = pill_y - 30 - mark_h
        canv.drawImage(self.mark_path, mark_x, mark_y, mark_w, mark_h, mask="auto", preserveAspectRatio=True)

        # 3. Tagline & Subtitles
        tag_y = mark_y - 28
        canv.setFillColor(BUTTER_GOLD)
        canv.setFont("Manrope-Bold", 18)
        canv.drawCentredString(cx, tag_y, "PEEL. PRESS. TOAST.")

        sub1_y = tag_y - 24
        canv.setFillColor(WHITE)
        canv.setFont("Manrope-Semi", 13)
        canv.drawCentredString(cx, sub1_y, "The Utensil-Free Breakfast Revolution")

        sub2_y = sub1_y - 22
        canv.setFillColor(ELECTRIC_LAVENDER)
        canv.setFont("Manrope-Bold", 10.5)
        canv.drawCentredString(cx, sub2_y, "COMMERCIAL BUSINESS PLAN & INVESTOR PROSPECTUS")

        # 4. Info Card
        card_w = min(W - 20, 460)
        card_h = 135
        card_x = cx - card_w / 2
        card_y = sub2_y - 34 - card_h
        canv.setFillColor(CARD_DARK)
        canv.setStrokeColor(BORDER_DARK)
        canv.setLineWidth(1.2)
        canv.roundRect(card_x, card_y, card_w, card_h, 10, stroke=1, fill=1)

        # Card top accent line
        canv.setFillColor(ELECTRIC_LAVENDER)
        canv.roundRect(card_x, card_y + card_h - 4, card_w, 4, 2, stroke=0, fill=1)

        # Card content (Two columns)
        col1_x = card_x + 24
        col2_x = card_x + card_w / 2 + 10
        row_start = card_y + card_h - 28
        row_gap = 24

        def draw_meta_row(x, y, label, val):
            canv.setFillColor(LAVENDER_SOFT)
            canv.setFont("Manrope-Semi", 8.5)
            canv.drawString(x, y + 10, label.upper())
            canv.setFillColor(WHITE)
            canv.setFont("Manrope-Bold", 10.5)
            canv.drawString(x, y - 2, val)

        draw_meta_row(col1_x, row_start, "Prepared By", "Jacob")
        draw_meta_row(col1_x, row_start - row_gap - 10, "Date", "30 September 2026")
        draw_meta_row(col1_x, row_start - 2*(row_gap + 10), "Industry / Category", "FMCG — Ambient Spreads")

        draw_meta_row(col2_x, row_start, "Live Digital Platform", "stamp-spreads.vercel.app")
        draw_meta_row(col2_x, row_start - row_gap - 10, "Source Repository", "github.com/JacobCrume/stamp-spreads")
        draw_meta_row(col2_x, row_start - 2*(row_gap + 10), "Commercial Status", "Ready for Production Pilot")

        # 5. Four Flavor Pills
        flav_y = card_y - 32
        flavors = [
            ("Salted Butter", BUTTER_GOLD),
            ("Raspberry", RASPBERRY_RUBY),
            ("Yeast Extract", YEAST_MALT),
            ("Roasted Peanut", PEANUT_AMBER)
        ]
        total_pills_w = 4 * 105 + 3 * 10
        f_start_x = cx - total_pills_w / 2
        for idx, (fl_name, fl_col) in enumerate(flavors):
            fx = f_start_x + idx * 115
            canv.setFillColor(DEEP_PURPLE)
            canv.setStrokeColor(BORDER_DARK)
            canv.setLineWidth(0.8)
            canv.roundRect(fx, flav_y, 105, 20, 10, stroke=1, fill=1)
            # Dot
            canv.setFillColor(fl_col)
            canv.circle(fx + 12, flav_y + 10, 4, stroke=0, fill=1)
            # Name
            canv.setFillColor(WHITE)
            canv.setFont("Manrope-Semi", 8)
            canv.drawString(fx + 22, flav_y + 6.5, fl_name)

        # 6. Bottom footer note
        canv.setFillColor(LAVENDER_SOFT)
        canv.setFont("Manrope", 8.5)
        canv.drawCentredString(cx, 24, "Auckland, New Zealand  •  Strictly Confidential  •  Version 1.0")

def draw_cover_bg(canv, doc):
    canv.saveState()
    canv.setFillColor(PRIMARY_DARK)
    canv.rect(0, 0, A4[0], A4[1], stroke=0, fill=1)

    # Decorative background glows
    canv.setFillColor(DEEP_PURPLE)
    canv.circle(A4[0] / 2, A4[1] * 0.65, 280, stroke=0, fill=1)
    canv.setFillColor(PRIMARY_DARK)
    canv.circle(A4[0] / 2, A4[1] * 0.65, 240, stroke=0, fill=1)

    canv.restoreState()

register_fonts()
mark_path = Path("/tmp/test_mark.png")
px_w, px_h = create_cover_wordmark(ROOT / "brand" / "logo.png", mark_path)

doc = BaseDocTemplate("/tmp/test_cover.pdf", pagesize=A4)
frame = Frame(36, 36, A4[0]-72, A4[1]-72, id="c", showBoundary=0)
template = PageTemplate(id="c", frames=[frame], onPage=draw_cover_bg)
doc.addPageTemplates([template])
doc.build([CoverFlowable(str(mark_path), px_w, px_h)])
print("Built /tmp/test_cover.pdf successfully")
EOF

    img = PILImage.open(src).convert("RGBA")

def create_cover_wordmark(src: Path, dest: Path) -> tuple[int, int]:
    img = PILImage.open(src).convert("RGBA")
    arr = np.array(img).astype(float)
    diff = np.sqrt((arr[:, :, 0] - 226)**2 + (arr[:, :, 1] - 75)**2 + (arr[:, :, 2] - 255)**2)
    alpha = np.clip((diff - 20) / 60.0, 0, 1)
    out = np.zeros((img.height, img.width, 4), dtype=np.uint8)
    out[:, :, 0] = 226
    out[:, :, 1] = 75
    out[:, :, 2] = 255
    out[:, :, 3] = (alpha * 255).astype(np.uint8)
    res = PILImage.fromarray(out)
    bbox = res.getbbox()
    pad = 20
    box = (max(0, bbox[0]-pad), max(0, bbox[1]-pad), min(img.width, bbox[2]+pad), min(img.height, bbox[3]+pad))
    cropped = res.crop(box)
    cropped.save(dest)
    return cropped.size

        mark_x = cx - mark_w / 2
        canv.drawImage(self.mark_path, mark_x, mark_y, mark_w, mark_h, mask="auto", preserveAspectRatio=True)

    def draw(self):
        canv = self.canv
        W = self.avail_width

        pill_w = 190
        pill_h = 24
        pill_y = y_anchor + 60
        canv.setFillColor(self.scheme["tertiary"])
        canv.roundRect(0, pill_y, pill_w, pill_h, 12, stroke=0, fill=1)
        canv.setFillColor(self.scheme["primary"])
        canv.setFont("Manrope-Bold", 9)
        canv.drawCentredString(pill_w / 2, pill_y + 7.5, f"SECTION {self.num}  •  {self.kicker}")

        # 2. Main Title
        canv.setFillColor(WHITE)
        canv.setFont("Manrope-Bold", 32)
        canv.drawString(0, y_anchor + 12, self.title)

        # 3. Flat Accent Rule
        canv.setFillColor(self.scheme["primary"])
        canv.rect(0, y_anchor, W, 3, stroke=0, fill=1)

        # 4. Subtitle / Theme descriptor
        if self.subtitle:

Analyzing design specifications for the business plan. Initial focus is on the cover page: determining color scheme (Deep Night Ink), centered wordmark styling with subtext (Electric Lavender), and the placement and text of the document title (white). Proceeding to analyze section page requirements.


The section page will use the secondary color for a full bleed background. The title and subtitle will use the primary color and Manrope font, with specified sizes and no line separating them. The section page footer will contain the primary color wordmark in the bottom-left and the page number in the bottom-right.

Content pages will have a white background with dark ink text. The title will utilize the primary color. 48 RIGHT = 48 FRAME_BOTTOM = 54 FRAME_TOP = 50 # 4 Authentic Flavour Schemes from website/src/lib/theme.svelte.ts SCHEMES = [ { "id": "yeast", "name": "Yeast Extract", "primary": HexColor("#E24BFF"), raw.split(":", 1) fields[key.strip()] = value.strip() index += 1 current["blocks"].append(("figure", fields)) index += 1 continue if stripped == ":::row": flush() if current is None: raise stripped.startswith("# "): index += 1 continue prose.append(line) index += 1 flush() return sections def prose_word_counts(sections: list[dict]) -> tuple[int, dict[str, int]]: per: dict[str, int] = {} total = 0 for section in sections: parts: list[str] = [] for block in section["blocks"]: if block[0] != "prose": continue for line in block[1].splitlines(): if line.strip().startswith("|"): continue parts.append(line) raw = "\n".join(parts) raw = re.sub(r"\[([^\]]+)\]\([^)]+\)", r"\1", raw) raw = raw.replace("**", "").replace("*", "").replace("`", "") words = raw.split() per[section["title"]] = len(words) total += len(words) return total, per def xml_text(text: str) -> str: text = text.replace("&", "&").replace("<", "<").replace(">", ">") def soften(match: re.Match[str]) -> str: url = match.group(0) plain = url.replace("&", "&") limit = 480 def wide(value: str) -> float: return pdfmetrics.stringWidth(value, "Manrope", 10.0) if wide(plain) <= limit: return url pieces = url.split("/") lines: list[str] = [] current = pieces[0] for piece in pieces[1:]: addition = "/" + piece trial = (current + addition).replace("&", "&") if current and wide(trial) > limit: lines.append(current) current = addition else: current += addition if current: lines.append(current) return "
".join(lines) text = re.sub(r"https?://[^\s<]+", soften, text) text = re.sub(r"\*\*([^*]+)\*\*", r"\1", text) return text def body_paragraph(text: str, style: ParagraphStyle): xml = xml_text(text) kind = SolidParagraph if "http" in xml else Paragraph return kind(xml, style) def prepare_image(src: Path, dest: Path) -> tuple[int, int]: image = PILImage.open(src) if image.mode in ("RGBA", "LA") or (image.mode == "P" and "transparency" in image.info): image = image.convert("RGBA") base = PILImage.new("RGBA", image.size, (248, 250, 252, 255)) flat = PILImage.alpha_composite(base, image).convert("RGB") else: flat = image.convert("RGB") flat.save(dest, "PNG") return flat.size def create_recolored_wordmark(src: Path, dest: Path, rgb: tuple[int, int, int]) -> tuple[int, int]: """Extract smooth, anti-aliased STAMP wordmark recolored to rgb.""" img = PILImage.open(src).convert("RGBA") arr = np.array(img).astype(float) diff = np.sqrt( (arr[:, :, 0] - 226) ** 2 + (arr[:, :, 1] - 75) ** 2 + (arr[:, :, 2] - 255) ** 2 ) alpha = np.clip((diff - 20) / 60.0, 0, 1) out = np.zeros((img.height, img.width, 4), dtype=np.uint8) out[:, :, 0] = rgb[0] out[:, :, 1] = rgb[1] out[:, :, 2] = rgb[2] out[:, :, 3] = (alpha * 255).astype(np.uint8) res = PILImage.fromarray(out) bbox = res.getbbox() if bbox: pad = 20 box = ( max(0, bbox[0] - pad), max(0, bbox[1] - pad), min(img.width, bbox[2] + pad), min(img.height, bbox[3] + pad), ) cropped = res.crop(box) else: cropped = res cropped.save(dest, "PNG") return cropped.size # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- # FLOWABLES & PAGE LAYOUTS # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- class MinimalCover(Flowable): """Ultra-minimalist cover page strictly matching user specifications.""" def __init__(self, mark_path: str, px_w: int, px_h: int): super().__init__() self.mark_path = mark_path self.px_w = px_w self.px_h = px_h def wrap(self, avail_width, avail_height): self.avail_width = avail_width self.avail_height = avail_height return avail_width, avail_height def draw(self): canv = self.canv W = self.avail_width H = self.avail_height cx = W / 2 # Centered STAMP Wordmark mark_w = 400 mark_h = mark_w * self.px_h / self.px_w center_y = H / 2 mark_y = center_y + 10 mark_x = cx - args.CodeContent:
"""Market figures for the Stamp commercial business plan.

Figures are branded strictly following Stamp's visual identity:
- Manrope typography (Bold, Semi, Medium)
- Stamp brand palette: Deep Night Ink (#240340), Deep Solid Purple (#3B0764),
  Electric Lavender (#E24BFF), Wild Raspberry (#FF467A), Roasted Peanut (#FF8C30),
  Electric Butter (#FFD640)
- High-contrast, clean minimalist layout with subtle grids and bold data callouts
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib.font_manager as fm
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

OUT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "figures"
DATA = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "sales-clean.csv"
FONT_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "brand" / "fonts"

# Register Manrope fonts with Matplotlib
for weight in ["400", "500", "600", "700"]:
    font_file = FONT_DIR / f"Manrope-{weight}.ttf"
    if font_file.is_file():
        fm.fontManager.addfont(str(font_file))

plt.rcParams["font.family"] = "Manrope"

CATEGORY_ORDER = [
    "Breakfast Cereals",
    "Nutritional Cereal Bars",
    "Spreads",
    "Liquid Breakfasts",
]

TIER_ORDER = ["Value", "Standard", "Premium"]

BRAND_COLOURS = {
    "Breakfast Cereals": "#3B0764",       # Deep Solid Purple
    "Nutritional Cereal Bars": "#FF8C30", # Peanut Ochre
    "Spreads": "#E24BFF",                 # Electric Lavender (highlighted)
    "Liquid Breakfasts": "#FF467A",       # Wild Raspberry
    "2022": "#3B0764",                    # Deep Solid Purple
    "2025": "#E24BFF",                    # Electric Lavender
}


def quarterly_revenue(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> None:
    quarters = sorted(frame["Date"].unique())
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10.5, 5.2), dpi=200)
    fig.patch.set_facecolor("white")
    ax.set_facecolor("white")

    for category in CATEGORY_ORDER:
        part = frame[frame["Category"] == category]
        series = (
            part.groupby("Date")["Revenue (Thousands NZD)"].sum().reindex(quarters).fillna(0)
            / 1000
        )
        is_spreads = category == "Spreads"
        ax.plot(
            quarters,
            series.values,
            label=f"{category} (Focus)" if is_spreads else category,
            color=BRAND_COLOURS[category],
            linewidth=3.2 if is_spreads else 1.8,
            alpha=1.0 if is_spreads else 0.75,
            zorder=5 if is_spreads else 3,
        )

    ax.set_title(
        "Quarterly Breakfast Category Revenue in New Zealand (2022–2025)",
        fontsize=13.5,
        fontweight="bold",
        color="#240340",
        pad=16,
    )
    ax.set_ylabel("Revenue (Million NZD)", fontsize=10.5, fontweight="bold", color="#475569", labelpad=10)
    ax.set_xlabel("Quarter", fontsize=10.5, fontweight="bold", color="#475569", labelpad=10)

    legend = ax.legend(
        frameon=True,
        facecolor="#F8FAFC",
        edgecolor="#E2E8F0",
        fontsize=9.5,
        loc="upper left",
    )
    for text in legend.get_texts():
        text.set_color("#1A1024")
        text.set_fontweight("bold")

    ax.tick_params(axis="x", labelrotation=45, colors="#475569", labelsize=9)
    ax.tick_params(axis="y", colors="#64748B", labelsize=9.5)
    ax.grid(axis="y", linestyle="--", alpha=0.4, color="#CBD5E1", zorder=0)
    ax.spines["top"].set_visible(False)
    ax.spines["right"].set_visible(False)
    ax.spines["left"].set_color("#E2E8F0")
    ax.spines["bottom"].set_color("#CBD5E1")

    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(OUT / "01-quarterly-revenue-by-category.png", dpi=200)
    plt.close(fig)


def tier_comparison(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> None:
    spreads = frame[frame["Category"] == "Spreads"].copy()
    spreads["year"] = spreads["Date"].str.slice(0, 4)
    part = spreads[spreads["year"].isin(["2022", "2025"])]
    totals = (
        part.groupby(["year", "Price Tier"])["Revenue (Thousands NZD)"].sum().unstack("year")
        / 1000
    )
    totals = totals.reindex(TIER_ORDER)

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8.5, 4.8), dpi=200)
    fig.patch.set_facecolor("white")
    ax.set_facecolor("white")

    positions = np.arange(len(TIER_ORDER))
    width = 0.35

    rects1 = ax.bar(
        positions - width / 2,
        totals["2022"],
        width=width,
        label="2022 Revenue",
        color=BRAND_COLOURS["2022"],
        edgecolor="none",
        zorder=3,
    )
    rects2 = ax.bar(
        positions + width / 2,
        totals["2025"],
        width=width,
        label="2025 Revenue",
        color=BRAND_COLOURS["2025"],
        edgecolor="none",
        zorder=3,
    )

    # Direct value annotations above each bar
    for rect in rects1:
        h = rect.get_height()
        ax.annotate(
            f"${h:.1f}M",
            (rect.get_x() + rect.get_width() / 2, h),
            xytext=(0, 5),
            textcoords="offset points",
            ha="center",
            va="bottom",
            fontsize=9.5,
            fontweight="bold",
            color="#3B0764",
        )

    for rect in rects2:
        h = rect.get_height()
        ax.annotate(
            f"${h:.1f}M",
            (rect.get_x() + rect.get_width() / 2, h),
            xytext=(0, 5),
            textcoords="offset points",
            ha="center",
            va="bottom",
            fontsize=9.5,
            fontweight="bold",
            color="#A21CAF",
        )

    ax.set_xticks(positions)
    ax.set_xticklabels(TIER_ORDER, fontsize=11, fontweight="bold", color="#1A1024")
    ax.set_ylabel("Revenue (Million NZD)", fontsize=10.5, fontweight="bold", color="#475569", labelpad=10)
    ax.set_title(
        "New Zealand Spreads Category Revenue by Price Tier (2022 vs 2025)",
        fontsize=13,
        fontweight="bold",
        color="#240340",
        pad=16,
    )

    ax.grid(axis="y", linestyle="--", alpha=0.4, color="#CBD5E1", zorder=0)
    ax.spines["top"].set_visible(False)
    ax.spines["right"].set_visible(False)
    ax.spines["left"].set_color("#E2E8F0")
    ax.spines["bottom"].set_color("#CBD5E1")
    ax.tick_params(axis="y", colors="#64748B", labelsize=9.5)
    ax.tick_params(axis="x", colors="#1A1024", length=0)
    ax.set_ylim(0, max(totals.max()) * 1.18)

    legend = ax.legend(
        frameon=True,
        facecolor="#F8FAFC",
        edgecolor="#E2E8F0",
        fontsize=9.5,
        loc="upper left",
    )
    for text in legend.get_texts():
        text.set_color("#1A1024")
        text.set_fontweight("bold")

    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(OUT / "02-spreads-revenue-by-tier-2022-vs-2025.png", dpi=200)
    plt.close(fig)


def price_distribution(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> None:
    spreads = frame[
        (frame["Category"] == "Spreads")
        & (frame["Market Segment"] == "Branded")
        & frame["price_usable"]
        & frame["price_per_100g"].notna()
    ].copy()

    sku = spreads.groupby(["Product Name", "Brand", "Weight"], as_index=False)[
        "price_per_100g"
    ].median()

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8.5, 4.8), dpi=200)
    fig.patch.set_facecolor("white")
    ax.set_facecolor("white")

    # Histogram with Stamp brand colors
    n, bins, patches = ax.hist(
        sku["price_per_100g"],
        bins=26,
        color="#240340",
        edgecolor="white",
        linewidth=1.2,
        zorder=3,
    )

    for patch in patches:
        if patch.get_x() >= 5.0:
            patch.set_facecolor("#3B0764")

    # Stamp price line
    stamp_price = 6.25
    ax.axvline(stamp_price, color="#E24BFF", linestyle="-", linewidth=2.6, zorder=4)

    # 90th percentile benchmark line
    p90 = sku["price_per_100g"].quantile(0.9)
    ax.axvline(p90, color="#FF8C30", linestyle="--", linewidth=1.8, zorder=4)

    # Annotations
    ylim = ax.get_ylim()[1]
    ax.text(
        stamp_price + 0.15,
        ylim * 0.88,
        "STAMP: $6.25 / 100 g\nFormat Innovation Premium",
        fontsize=9.5,
        fontweight="bold",
        color="#A21CAF",
        va="top",
    )

    ax.text(
        p90 - 0.15,
        ylim * 0.72,
        f"90th Percentile: ${p90:.2f} / 100 g",
        fontsize=8.5,
        fontweight="bold",
        color="#C2410C",
        ha="right",
        va="top",
    )

    ax.set_xlabel("Shelf Price per 100 g (NZD)", fontsize=10.5, fontweight="bold", color="#475569", labelpad=8)
    ax.set_ylabel("Number of Branded Spread SKUs", fontsize=10.5, fontweight="bold", color="#475569", labelpad=8)
    ax.set_title(
        "Shelf Price Distribution Across 154 Branded New Zealand Spread SKUs",
        fontsize=13,
        fontweight="bold",
        color="#240340",
        pad=16,
    )

    ax.grid(axis="y", linestyle="--", alpha=0.4, color="#CBD5E1", zorder=0)
    ax.spines["top"].set_visible(False)
    ax.spines["right"].set_visible(False)
    ax.spines["left"].set_color("#E2E8F0")
    ax.spines["bottom"].set_color("#CBD5E1")
    ax.tick_params(axis="y", colors="#64748B", labelsize=9.5)
    ax.tick_params(axis="x", colors="#1A1024", labelsize=9.5)

    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(OUT / "03-branded-spreads-price-per-100g.png", dpi=200)
    plt.close(fig)

    quantiles = sku["price_per_100g"].quantile([0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9])
    print("branded spread SKUs", len(sku))
    print(quantiles.to_string())
    print("min", round(sku["price_per_100g"].min(), 2), "max", round(sku["price_per_100g"].max(), 2))


def main() -> None:
    OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    frame = pd.read_csv(DATA)
    quarterly_revenue(frame)
    tier_comparison(frame)
    price_distribution(frame)
    print("Successfully regenerated branded figures in data/figures/")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
